Wider Sports News.title: Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’
Wider Sports News.summary: Two-time gold medal winner praises investment in the sport as World Triathlon moves to create centralised tour. The post Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’ appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Two-time Olympic triathlon champion Alistair Brownlee believes the sport is in an incredibly healthy position but thinks that greater consolidation may be needed. Triathlon was admitted to the Olympic Games in 2000, a development which catalysed participation levels and, more recently, has led to the creation of several major competitions and significant private investment.

These include SuperTri and the Professional Triathletes Organisation (PTO), which have joined the most established Ironman and World Triathlon circuits. However, apart from World Triathlon’s events, which include the Olympic competitions, all of these are privately run with varying levels of official recognition from the world governing body.

Barely a month after Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup at MetLife Stadium in New York, the Premier League returns this week after a summer that saw 182 of its players compete at soccer’s flagship international tournament.

Wider Sports News.summary: With three US races, quirky sponsorship designations, and a Brad Pitt-led Hollywood movie under its belt, the American influence on F1 is unquestionable. But Liam Parker argues the term ‘Americanisation’ is pejorative and should instead be viewed as the modernisation of the sport. The post Why F1 believes ‘Americanisation’ is helping modernise the sport appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The new cars are ruining the sport. The racing is too processional. The sport was better ‘back in my day’. These are just some of the accusations levelled at Formula One following the most recent alterations to the sport’s regulations.

True, they are the most significant modifications in a generation, but fan discontent following rule changes is nothing new. Whether it’s the start of the ground effect era in 2022, the introduction of hybrid engines in 2014, or the double diffuser drama of 2009, Formula One starting afresh and fan protests often go hand in hand – and that’s just this century.

Wider Sports News.summary: Strategic initiative will equip employees across every division with AI capabilities designed to enhance creativity, accelerate operations and deliver greater value for clients. The post GSE Worldwide partners with Extraordinary AI to accelerate enterprise-wide AI strategy and innovation appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
New York (July 22, 2026) – GSE Worldwide (GSE) today announced a strategic partnership with Extraordinary AI (EAI), an AI advisory firm specialising in enterprise AI adoption, to launch a firmwide initiative designed to embed artificial intelligence across the agency’s operations. The investment reflects GSE’s belief that AI will fundamentally reshape how sports and entertainment agencies operate by enhancing creativity, improving efficiency, and enabling teams to deliver smarter, more personalised solutions for clients. Through the partnership, GSE is proactively equipping its workforce with the knowledge, tools, and strategic framework needed to lead that transformation.

Through the initiative, employees from across GSE’s business will participate in a structured engagement that combines AI education, hands-on workshops and collaborative development sessions focused on identifying practical applications for artificial intelligence within the agency’s day-to-day operations. Rather than implementing off-the-shelf solutions, participants will develop AI-powered workflows and processes tailored specifically to GSE’s business and the needs of its clients.

Wider Sports News.body:
A consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has agreed to buy almost a third of Premier League giants Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group (FSG) in a deal that values the club at a reported UK£5.5 billion (US$7.45 billion).

The 1892 Holdings consortium, the name of which refers to the year the Merseyside club were founded, will acquire a 30 per cent stake worth UK£1.65 billion (US$2.24 billion) and will have the option to take full control should FSG decide to sell in the future.

Wider Sports News.title: GSE Worldwide launches GSE advisory, names Michael Brown executive vice president
Wider Sports News.summary: New advisory practice builds upon GSE's existing brand services to help organisations maximise their investment in sports. The post GSE Worldwide launches GSE advisory, names Michael Brown executive vice president appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
New York (July 28, 2026) – GSE Worldwide (GSE), a leader in sports and entertainment marketing, event production and talent management, today announced the launch of GSE Advisory, a new advisory practice that expands the company’s existing brand-facing capabilities by providing senior-level strategic guidance to brands, rights holders, investors and sports organizations navigating growth through sports. The company also announced the appointment of industry veteran Michael Brown as executive vice president, GSE Advisory, effective July 27.

Building upon GSE’s existing brand services, the launch of GSE Advisory marks the next phase in GSE’s continued evolution, adding a dedicated advisory practice to the company’s existing capabilities across talent representation, experiential marketing, hospitality, and live events. By combining strategic guidance with direct access to the people, platforms, and experiences that shape today’s sports landscape, GSE Advisory will help brands answer critical questions around where to invest, which partnerships create the greatest value, and how to maximize their investments in sports.

Wider Sports News.title: What the LA Lakers’ sunning quickfire US$12.5bn sale says about the state of US sports investment
Wider Sports News.summary: Less than 12 months after being officially confirmed as the owner of the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers, Mark Walter is ready to sell to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner. The billionaire’s shock exit is set to generate a remarkable short-term profit – and a lot of questions. The post What the LA Lakers’ sunning quickfire US$12.5bn sale says about the state of US sports investment appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
For the second time in two years, the Los Angeles Lakers are about to become the most expensive team in world sport. Pending approval from the league board, the 17-time National Basketball Association (NBA) champions will sell for a reported US$12.5 billion to a group led by former Disney chief executive Bob Iger and Josh Kushner – venture capitalist, younger brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, and recent associate of Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

It is an extraordinary development. The deal comes less than a year after current owner Mark Walter was cleared to take the franchise out of the hands of the Buss family, when his purchase of a controlling stake valued the Lakers at US$10 billion.

Rugby.title: Rassie's tribute to Damian de Allende ahead of 100th Sprinboks Test
Rugby.summary: Damian de Allende's name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team.
Rugby.body:
Damian de Allende’s name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team. The bruising inside centre will become just the 10th Springboks centurion when the whistle blows at Ellis Park, with Jean de Villiers the only midfielder before him to reach the milestone.

The achievement puts even more on the line in Saturday’s historic Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, in which De Allende will link up with familiar midfield partner Jesse Kriel to take on New Zealand’s Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea.

Rugby.title: Jona Nareki on the All Blacks' new 'beast', Otago's new star and Wellington's woes
Rugby.summary: For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable.
Rugby.body:
For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable. But after a narrow 19-15 loss to Canterbury in Dunedin on Sunday, the prospect of a Palmerston North stumble was real. The visitors trailed 24-7 after 45 minutes and 27-12 with ten minutes left.

“I’m getting older, in rugby age only. I’m not proud of my yellow card coming in the side. I owned one for the team,” Nareki laughed with RugbyPass. “Watching the game from the sideline, I noticed we weren’t winning contact at all while Manawatu went two phases the same way then switched short side to expose us. Once we fixed that, they became easier to defend against.

Rugby.title: The All Blacks' selection policy just got a lot less sentimental
Rugby.summary: Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.
Rugby.body:
I have to say I’m relieved and optimistic. The first name I looked for, in the All Blacks’ 23 to play South Africa at Ellis Park, was Beauden Barrett. Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.

So, there’s no Beauden Barrett and no Rieko Ioane in the 23 either. Both are hugely encouraging signs that, while there’s a cast of thousands on this tour, Test caps will still have to be earned.

Rugby.title: 'Borderline Personality Disorder is my superpower'
Rugby.summary: Wales' Donna Rose tells BBC Sport how rugby union has helped her manage Borderline Personality Disorder.
Rugby.body:
Tighthead prop Donna Rose has had an unforgettable 12 months on the rugby pitch. Last year, she proudly represented Wales at her second World Cup before helping Saracens lift the Premiership Women's Rugby title in June.

From the outside looking in, she is known as a hard-hitting player with a big personality. But off the pitch, few see the daily struggles the 35-year-old copes with. Rose has borderline personality disorder (BPD), a mental health condition that causes unstable moods, behaviours and relationships.

Rugby.title: 'I've been waiting for this': Roigard on 'finally' getting another crack at Boks
Rugby.summary: Fit at long last and selected to start in his familiar No.9 jersey, Roigard says his Springboks sequel has been a long time coming.
Rugby.body:
A run of poorly timed injuries has kept Cam Roigard from lacing up his boots in the famous All Blacks v Springboks rivalry for every showdown since his debut season, with just a brief showing off the bench in his rookie year the exception. This weekend at Ellis Park, the star halfback will finally get his shot at the world champs.

Roigard’s lone showing against South Africa came in a historic defeat at Twickenham ahead of the 2023 Rugby World Cup. Then just 22 years of age, the rising star produced a brilliant solo effort try, one that saved his side from a historic goose egg.

Rugby.title: Wallaroos teen relishes start opposite all-time Black Ferns great
Rugby.summary: Waiaria Ellis is both nervous and excited about the opportunity to line up opposite one of the all-time greats in Ruahei Demant.
Rugby.body:
Waiaria Ellis is both nervous and excited about the opportunity to line up opposite one of the all-time greats in Ruahei Demant, with the teenager set for a maiden start at fly-half for the Wallaroos against the Black Ferns on Saturday.

Ellis has previously played in the outside backs for the Wallaroos, debuting for the national team as a winger against the Black Ferns in Wellington last July. But the utility back will wear the No. 10 jersey this weekend, in what will be the 100th Test in Wallaroos history.

Rugby.title: ‘Inspire the next generation’: Northland end near 50-year Shield wait
Rugby.summary: Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional at full-time.
Rugby.body:
Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional after a famous 35-12 win over Canterbury that was unforgettable in more ways than one.

It was a history-making night at One NZ Stadium for the Taniwha, who hadn’t beaten Canterbury in Christchurch since the late 1980s. All Blacks Sevens star Rob Rush shone bright as Northland ended a long-running search for the Shield as well, which dates back to the 1970s.

It was a history-making night at One NZ Stadium for the Taniwha, who hadn’t beaten Canterbury in Christchurch since the late 1980s. All Blacks Sevens star Rob Rush shone bright as Northland ended a long-running search for the Shield as well, which dates back to the 1970s.

Rugby.title: ‘We can win this game’: Wallaroos chase historic first against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: 30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time.
Rugby.body:
30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time. But the Aussies aren’t shying away from their shot at history, heading across the ditch with the belief “that we can win this game.”

The Wallaroos fell to a 35-point defeat in the last meeting between the rivals on April 25, in a historic Anzac Day fixture between the sides on the Sunshine Coast. Siokapesi Palu Sekona was the sole try-scorer for the Wallaroos, as the Black Ferns retained the O’Reilly Cup.

Rugby.title: Northampton Saints' Archie McParland set for crunch talks over club future
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract. Saints have started to tie down their players who are out of contract at the end of the forthcoming season and have already made England star Tommy Freeman the highest-paid winger in the league.

They are also set to meet with McParland’s Stowe School team-mate Henry Pollock’s advisors to try to thrash out a new deal that won’t be cheap, even though it is likely to fall short of the headline-grabbing £1 million that his commercial advisor, Eddie Hearn, thinks he is worth.

Rugby.title: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games Fanatik
Rugby.body:
Australia's Rugby Sevens programs will relocate to a new state-of-the-art training facility at Brisbane's Ballymore Stadium complex ahead of the 2032 Olympics, the Queensland government announced on Thursday. The major infrastructure development marks a strategic shift for national rugby operations in Australia.

The new "Teams in Gold Facility" is set to be constructed as part of the broader redevelopment of Ballymore, historically recognized as the spiritual home of rugby union in Queensland. Once construction is complete, both national Sevens teams will move their base from New South Wales to their new Queensland home.

Rugby.body:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has revealed that captain Siya Kolisi was available to face the All Blacks this weekend at Ellis Park in the first match of the Greatest Rivalry series, but the coaching team opted against selecting him.

It was originally feared that the 100-cap veteran would miss a large chunk, if not all, of the highly-anticipated series after picking up a hamstring injury in the Springboks’ 17-10 victory over Argentina earlier this month. However, Erasmus gave an upbeat update earlier this week on the injury status of both Kolisi and loosehead prop Ox Nche, saying they were both in contention to face the All Blacks in Johannesburg.

Rugby.summary: Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won't enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won’t enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series. The former Springbok captain, who led South Africa during New Zealand’s landmark 1996 series win on South African soil, believes Rassie Erasmus’ current world champions are primed to turn the tables 30 years on, backing the Boks to claim a dominant victory – with a caveat.

Speaking in Johannesburg at the launch of the new RGR trophy alongside former All Blacks skipper Sean Fitzpatrick, Teichmann said the memories of that painful 1996 defeat still remain fresh.

Rugby.summary: Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season.
Rugby.body:
Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season. The 23-year-old spent the past year-and-a-half at Ashton Gate, making his Gallagher PREM debut against Newcastle Red Bulls in April, but has had limited game time in the West Country.

The step down to England’s second division will see Cripps reunite with Warriors boss Matt Everard, whom he was coached by earlier in his career at Wasps. Worcester will get their title defence underway in just under a month, hosting Bedford Blues on Saturday, September 19, in what will be a repeat of last season’s final.

Rugby.title: Sana Govender: The Leinster head coach who came by way of Gdansk and Skibbereen
Rugby.summary: When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad.
Rugby.body:
When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad. It was the same case for Stacey Flood, when she started against Connacht last weekend. All three women have proudly represented Ireland in sevens and XVs, over the past few years [Flood made her senior sevens bow in 2015] yet were part of a large crop winning Leinster debuts.

The drive to get meaningful games into the four senior provinces has led to the recent prominence of the Vodafone Interprovincial Championship. The big stars missed out, last season, as they were on Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 duty, in England. For the current campaign, there have been a raft of overdue debuts.

Rugby.title: Match official appointments locked in for WXV Global Series and Challenger
Rugby.summary: French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series presented by Mitsubishi Electric. She joins Matthew Carley (England), Aimee Barrett-Theron (South Africa) and Hollie Davidson (Scotland) in reaching the landmark this year, and is the fifth French official to achieve the feat.

Groizeleau is one of 10 Emirates Match Officials appointed by World Rugby to take charge of the 30 WXV Global Series 2026 fixtures taking place across 13 counties. The 37-year-old will take charge of the opening game of the WXV Global Series campaign between England and Australia in Salford and hit her half-century the following month when she takes charge of Canada’s clash with the Red Roses in Toronto.

Rugby.title: Who is best equipped to strike first in the Greatest Rivalry showdown?
Rugby.summary: Are the world champion Springboks or new-look All Blacks in pole position to win their hugely anticipated first Test on Saturday?
Rugby.body:
“Every battle is won or lost before it is fought”. That pithy saying by the Chinese warrior-philosopher Sun-Tzu has become an axiom of modern sport at the elite level. The winning tends to consist of the preparation: the logistics on the approach-road to battle, the detail of the planning, the precision of the fore-knowledge of the strengths and weaknesses on both sides, observed without bias.

That is the process Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie, the rival head coaches of South Africa and New Zealand, will be fine-tuning now. The battle will only be fought at 17:10 on Saturday at Ellis Park, but there are myriad is to be dotted and ts to be crossed before then – in selection, in game planning, and in physical and mental training.

That is the process Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie, the rival head coaches of South Africa and New Zealand, will be fine-tuning now. The battle will only be fought at 17:10 on Saturday at Ellis Park, but there are myriad is to be dotted and ts to be crossed before then – in selection, in game planning, and in physical and mental training.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Read says Argentina gave the 'blueprint' for Boks
Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago.
Rugby.body:
Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago. Los Pumas hosted a strong South Africa side, although missing a host of topline stars, and were able to trouble them in their 17-10 loss, missing the chance to draw level with the final play of the game.

They led 10-3 for most of the first half and created a number of opportunities out wide through a varied attacking game that implemented chips and cross-field kicks. “Even though they [South Africa] didn’t put anything on the table in Argentina, Argentina showed us exactly how we should try to beat the Springboks,” Read said on The Good, The Bad & Rugby ANZ podcast.

Rugby.title: 'Not here for a sugar hit': Waratahs expect sustained success from 'proven winner' Cheika
Rugby.summary: NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach.
Rugby.body:
From the board down to the players and his assistants, all NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach. A proven force of nature, “Cyclone Cheika” will officially arrive at Daceyville in November charged with restoring the Waratahs to the glory days after three years without a Super Rugby Pacific finals appearance and a decade of under-achieving since he left the first time.

The firebrand mentor led the Waratahs to their one and only championship in 2014, while his abrasive style has also brought success to almost every team he’s coached. Cheika also coached Leinster to European Cup glory, Argentina to the World Cup semi-finals for the first time in 2023 and, as an assistant to Trent Robinson, has helped put the Sydney Roosters on track to claiming this year’s NRL minor premiership.

This was all just a minor subplot in a season where England’s results took a dramatic dive.

Rugby.title: All Blacks and Springboks agree to drawn series scenario
Rugby.summary: The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw. Wednesday afternoon’s trophy launch event in Johannesburg revealed the decision, as former Springboks captain Gary Teichmann carried one half of the sculptural trophy through a crowd and onto the stage, followed shortly after by former All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick with the other half.

Once on stage, the pair pressed the two pieces of the trophy together, revealing how magnets join them to form a single trophy, which would be handed to the winner of the series should either side claim at least three wins.

Rugby.title: Why Rassie’s next Bok generation could be the greatest ever
Rugby.summary: The Springbok dynasty doesn't look like it is going to disappear any time soon and it could, in fact, get even stronger in future
Rugby.body:
I’m positively hyperventilating about The Greatest Rivalry Test Series and it has my mind doing overtime as to how many ways it could go. It may be a heatwave here in the UK but over in South Africa, it’s piping hot for another reason. As ever, when it comes to rugby, there is no off-switch and this is what has been on my mind over the last month.

Sometimes the “next generation” can be a bit of letdown. Whether it’s people or products, the next in line doesn’t always mean an improvement. If you’ve ever spent a £1,000 on a new phone in recent years, or you’re acquainted with royal history over the past 1,000 years, you’ll know succession doesn’t always equal success — King John of England was arguably the iPhone 6 Plus of monarchs. However, the next generation of Rassie’s Springboks could arguably be the best to ever do it. They simply have to be, and for one reason: if you aren’t an almost generational-level player, you simply don’t get to play in the Test team proper.

They will play Brazil ‘A’ squad in back-to-back fixtures in Sao Paolo on 24 and 29 August. Rugby.title: Jake White: I urge Rennie to make a huge call that won't go down well in NZ
Rugby.summary: The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning.
Rugby.body:
The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning. I’ll explain. If you were a rugby coach, and you were asked if you wanted to coach international rugby, the answer would be yes. Now, if you were then asked to pick any side in the world to coach most, without hesitation, would say South Africa, France, maybe England, but you can bet your bottom dollar New Zealand would be right up there. A year out from the World Cup, you’re asked where would your dream tour would be? South Africa, the year before the World Cup? Consider it done. For good measure, we’ll throw in a couple of friendlies, an extended 45-man squad and you can tour the Republic, play golf, go to game farms and have an incredible bonding opportunity. Oh, and we’ll make those warm-up games winnable and schedule the last game at altitude to replicate the first Test. Of course, you can play the Bulls. What’s not to like?

What I’m saying is Dave Rennie has nothing to complain about. It’s the perfect scenario. They are unbeaten. They have a new coach. They have renewed energy. They’ve been given the opportunity of an extended tour, playing the world champions, who are likely to be in their way in their quest to win a fourth World Cup, and they’re underdogs. They are in a helluva good place.

Rugby.title: Spain announce one-off Test against rising women's rugby nation
Rugby.summary: Spain's Las Leonas will play a one-off Test against the Springbok Women at the start of October.
Rugby.body:
Spain’s Las Leonas will play a one-off Test against the Springbok Women at the start of October. The fixture will take place shortly after the side has played WXV Global Series Challenger fixtures against Fiji, Samoa and Brazil in Hong Kong China.

Seville will host the match at its La Cartuja Sports Complex on Sunday 4 October. It will be the first time that Las Leonas have ever played a fixture in the city. In their release, Real Federación Española de Rugby [FER] claimed that their first home game of the season will be “crucial for the women’s national team’s objectives; with qualification for the 2029 World Cup in Australia potentially within reach this season”.

Rugby.title: Atlanta Lolohea: 'My rugby is the most settled it’s been'
Rugby.summary: Established in 1861, Westport is New Zealand's oldest European settlement on the West Coast. Best known as a coal-mining centre, Westport has a population of less than 5000.
Rugby.body:
Established in 1861, Westport is New Zealand’s oldest European settlement on the West Coast. Best known as a coal-mining centre, Westport has a population of less than 5000. Still, it produces big dreamers and champions, including Black Ferns hooker Atlanta Lolohea, named after the sprawling American city in Georgia; home to the world’s largest airport, the 1996 Olympic Games, and known for casinos, Coca-Cola, blues and hip-hop music. It is also where an older sister was performing when Lolohea was born.

Lolohea has played 11 Tests for New Zealand but only 13 Farah Palmer Cup games for Canterbury, winning 11, including a Premiership in 2022. For most of her career she has been an understudy to the more experienced Georgia Ponsonby. Could that be set to change?

Rugby.title: Asia Rugby Sevens Series returns with new contenders chasing title honours
Rugby.summary: The headlining event, the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to feature 12 women’s and 12 men’s teams.
Rugby.body:
August to October are set to be busy months in Asia, with the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series and U18s tournaments set to get underway across China and Sri Lanka. The headlining event, the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to feature 12 women’s and 12 men’s teams, with the two events taking place either side of the 2026 Asian Games taking in Aichi & Nagoya, Japan, which will also feature several sides.

Suzhou in China is set to host the first weekend of action on the final weekend of August, with the tournament set to feature two newly promoted sides in both the men’s and women’s tournaments.

Rugby.title: KCB send strong message to Kenya Nations 7s Circuit rivals
Rugby.summary: The domestic sevens competition in Kenya is heating up, with defending champions KCB sending a strong message to the rest of the competition.
Rugby.body:
The domestic sevens competition in Kenya is heating up, with defending champions KCB sending a strong message to the rest of the competition with victory at the Kabeberi 7s. Heading into the third leg of the National 7s Circuit, the official halfway point of the competition, the defending champions had claimed victory in the opening round at the Prinsloo Sevens, before collapsing to finish in fifth at the Dala Sevens a fortnight ago.

However, spearheaded by Kenyan HSBC SVNS sarts George Ooro and Mike Wekesa, KCB fired back emphatically at the RFUEA Grounds in Nairobi, sweeping through their pool stages and claiming the final in a tense 14-12 win over Strathmore Leos.

Rugby.title: ‘Score one try against the All Blacks and your life is made’: Three great Springbok tries v NZ
Rugby.summary: Thinus Delport, Richard Bands and Ricky Januarie all achieved rugby immortality with career-defining tries against New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
There are worse things than being remembered for the best ten seconds of your life. Richard Bands has won Currie Cups, played Test rugby for South Africa and built a second career teaching young props the mysteries of the scrum. More than two decades after his last Springbok appearance, none of that is usually the first thing people want to discuss.

“I’m more than chuffed,” Bands says. “In my career, I’ve created something that 23 years later, when I speak to people, they still can tell me exactly where they were watching that game, watching me score that try.”

Rugby.summary: Speculation around Ruby Tui's club future has been put to rest after she signed for JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby runners-up Trailfinders Women.
Rugby.body:
Speculation around Ruby Tui‘s club future has been put to rest after she signed for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby runners-up Trailfinders Women. Across the past two weeks the Black Ferns wing and Rugby World Cup 2021 winner teased that her time on a rugby pitch may not have been over on her social media channels.

In June the 34-year-old played her first game of 15-a-side rugby in almost a year for the Barbarians against Wales at Allianz Stadium. In an exclusive interview with The Telegraph, Tui confessed that it took some persuading from some women’s rugby greats to convince her not to hang up her boots: “My friends Portia Woodman-Wickliffe and Meg Jones helped me, [they] really had a massive input on making the decision.

Michael Cheika has been unveiled as the NSW Waratahs head coach ahead of the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season, more than a decade after leading the side to its maiden championship title back in 2014.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks fullback Damian McKenzie is heading in the right direction according to assistant coach Tana Umaga as he battles to be fit for the first Test at Ellis Park.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks fullback Damian McKenzie is heading in the right direction according to assistant coach Tana Umaga as he battles to be fit for the first Test at Ellis Park. Umaga confirmed McKenzie got through the required training block on Tuesday as he battles an ankle injury suffered against the Sharks in Durban.

“He was sharp today. He got through what he needed to get through. So, he’s trending well for a big one this weekend. So, that’s all we can ask,” Umaga told media. “Our medical staff has done a really good job, as well as our S&C, to make sure that they’re taking every precaution they can, but making sure that he puts his best foot forward to be available for the team.”

Rugby.summary: 2025 John Eales Medal winner Len Ikitau has been named in a 34-man Wallabies squad for Flight Centre Series Tests against Los Pumas.
Rugby.body:
2025 John Eales Medal winner Len Ikitau has been named in a 34-man Wallabies squad for Flight Centre Series Tests against Los Pumas in Argentina, overcoming an ankle injury that ruled the centre out of both matches against the Brave Blossoms.

Ikitau didn’t feature in the first match of the Les Kiss coaching era, which was a thrilling 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka. Both Ikitau and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii missed the Townsville Test, but the Wallabies still prevailed 56-17.

Rugby.summary: USA Eagles prop Charlie Abel has sealed a return to European rugby 10 years after first playing in France, signing with Pro D2 outfit Oyonnax Rugby.
Rugby.body:
USA Eagles prop Charlie Abel has sealed a return to European rugby 10 years after first playing in France, signing with Pro D2 outfit Oyonnax Rugby as a medical joker. The Australian-born front-rower has been added to the squad after tighthead Ali Oz picked up a hamstring injury.

Abel debuted for the USA national team during the inaugural World Rugby Nations Cup fixtures last month, coming off the bench in a win over Spain. The Eagles secured an unbeaten 3-0 record in July after sides all bound for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie reveals Rassie Erasmus turned down pre-match meeting with officials
Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie revealed that the coaches will not be having any pre-match meetings with the match officials after Rassie Erasmus declined.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie revealed that the coaches will not be having any pre-match meetings with the match officials after Rassie Erasmus declined the meeting. Under the new World Rugby protocols, head coaches may only meet with a referee before a Test match if both opposing head coaches accept the invitation and attend the meeting together.

Erasmus’ decision to decline the meeting appears at odds with the media approach adopted by the Springboks which has been to raise discussions around the laws. Jaco Peyper was brought out to a press conference to explain the 30-second formation rule, while assistant Felix Jones aired the grievances of the South African club teams had against the All Blacks.

Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs vice-captain Maisy Allen will join Canterbury for the upcoming Farah Palmer Cup campaign in New Zealand. The flanker – who won the last of her five caps for the Red Roses against the Black Ferns at WXV 1 in 2023 – will return to her JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club for the start of the English league season in November.

Canterbury, who were runners-up last year, start their season against the Auckland Storm in a fortnight’s time. She made 17 league appearances as Chiefs returned to the play-offs at the first time of asking. Across her 1231 match minutes, Allen scored 10 tries, carried the ball 153 times for 545 metres, beat 29 defenders, completed 249 tackles and won 15 turnovers.

Rugby.body:
Springboks assistant coach Felix Jones has raised concerns over the legality of the All Blacks‘ tactics after receiving feedback from the South African franchises. The All Blacks have faced the Stormers, the Sharks and the Bulls in the opening three matches of their Greatest Rivalry series, recording three victories in the process ahead of the first Test against Rassie Erasmus’ side on Saturday at Ellis Park.

Speaking to the media ahead of the much-anticipated encounter in Johannesburg, Jones revealed some of the feedback the Springboks have received from the franchises after their encounters with the All Blacks. The Bok coaching staff have seen plenty that confirmed their own observations from the Nations Championship, particularly in how New Zealand are looking to play, but Jones said “a couple of things caught the franchises out”.

Rugby.body:

Cheika has spent this season working as an assistant coach at the Sydney Roosters on a one-year deal, after returning to Australia following a spell in the Gallagher Prem with Leicester Tigers.

It is 11 years since Cheika, 59, left the Waratahs, whom he led to a Super Rugby title in 2014, to become the full-time Wallabies coach after having done both jobs for 12 months. Since then, they have reached only one semi-final.

Rugby.title: How do Australia fit both ‘fetchers’ in side? Could ‘McZano’ be next ‘Pooper’ combo?
Rugby.summary: With two outstanding opensides in Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano, Les Kiss has an enviable dilemma to navigate.
Rugby.body:
If there’s one common thread that can be traced through Australian rugby since the dawn of professionalism, it’s been the continual line of genuinely world-class, on-ball openside flankers.

It might even extend well beyond the advent of professionalism in the 1990s, if we’re honest, but there’s no denying the lineage since the game turned pro. It starts with David Wilson in the late 90s and quickly moves to George Smith in that period Australian fans knowingly refer to as the ‘Golden Years’, a period that hasn’t really been replicated since. Annoyingly.

Rugby.title: Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea reveals what has her ‘excited’ in Wallaroos camp
Rugby.summary: It has been seven years since Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea last played a Test match for the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
It has been seven years since Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea last played a Test match for the Wallaroos. Just a teenager when handed her first taste of international rugby, in the years since the powerful centre has curated her craft with Australia Sevens and picked up gold medals at the Rugby Sevens World Cup and Commonwealth Games in 2022. But now the 25-year-old has returned to her roots.

Back in the Wallaroos squad ahead of the team’s centenary Test – which will take place against the Black Ferns in Auckland this Saturday – Lefau-Fakaosilea is at the forefront of an ever-changing Australia side. Even if Michaela Leonard and Emily Chancellor remain from her last O’Reilly Cup outing.

Rugby.title: How has the dry weather affected rugby clubs?
Rugby.summary: BBC Sport examines how the drought conditions in England have affected rugby clubs.
Rugby.body:
"Although summers are getting a lot drier, this is by far the driest we've been," says Simon Johnson, the groundsman at National Two side Redruth. Sports pitches up and down the country have been affected by the lack of rainfall, with the south west of England being in a state of drought since the end of July.

A hosepipe ban was implemented earlier this month as little rain fell, causing difficulty for sports fields up and down the country. "The lack of rainfall has affected end-of-season renovations so grass seed hasn't germinated quite as quickly as it should have done," Johnson told BBC Radio Cornwall.

TV presenter Nick Knowles believes Cornish Pirates are capable of becoming a sustainable Prem club. The presenter of shows such as DIY SOS and National Lottery: Who Dares Wins invested in the Pirates earlier this month.

He is one of a number of new investors to join the Penzance-based Champ club over the past year or so. American firm Stonewood Capital Management took a stake in May to join a consortium of local businessmen who took over the club from long-serving owner Dick Evans in January 2025.

Rugby.summary: Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think. A squad for the two-Test tour – their first game is in San Salvador on August 29 – is likely to be named on Wednesday.

It’s understood Max Jorgensen, who limped off with sore ribs after a collision in the side’s big Townsville win over Japan on Saturday, will be fit to travel. Centres Len Ikitau (ankle) and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii (hamstring) are also firming for returns, giving their coach more welcome headaches after casting the net wide in his first two games in charge.

Rugby.summary: The offload specialist has made 132 professional appearances across stints at the Glasgow Warriors, Racing 92, Toulon and Castres, and won 68 Test caps.
Rugby.body:
Three-time World Cup player Leone Nakarawa is returning home to Fiji to play for the Drua in the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific competition. One of the most storied Flying Fijians of all time, Nakarawa is set to bring much-needed experience to the young Drua squad.

As well as being a part of three Rugby World Cup campaigns, including 2015 when he was selected in the official team of the tournament, the 38-year-old was part of their gold medal-winning sevens squad at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Rugby.title: Hansen forced to draft in two players ahead of ‘pressure’ Wallaroos clash
Rugby.summary: Following the Black Ferns' clash with the Wallaroos, they will travel to South Africa to feature in a double header with the All Blacks in Johannesburg on September 5.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has been forced to draft in two Black Ferns XV players ahead of their clash with the Wallaroos at Mt Smart Stadium on Saturday evening. The Black Ferns, who beat the Black Ferns XV 62-19 in Upper Hutt last Friday, will take on Australia in Auckland on Saturday to kick-start a busy international period for Hansen’s side.

The Wallaroos will head into the contest without their newly appointed head coach, as Sione Fukofuka is only taking the reins from January 2027. But for Hansen and the Black Ferns, the original squad has changed following the trial match, with both Tara Turner and Mo’omo’oga Palu picking up injuries that have made them unavailable for the weekend.

Rugby.title: Josh Moorby reveals All Blacks’ expectations of Boks amid style debate
Rugby.summary: There's been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend's showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks outside back Josh Moorby isn’t feeding into the narratives around the Springboks possibly slowing the game down ahead of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour. There’s been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend’s showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.

The All Blacks, who have preached a fast-paced contest, are clear in their intentions to take the game to the Springboks from the get-go in the first Test. One player who will welcome the All Blacks’ high ball-in-play attitude is Moorby, who dotted down for two tries against the Bulls in Pretoria, continuing his exceptional try-scoring form from the 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season.

Rugby.title: 'Always three truths': Rassie Erasmus and Jaco Peyper respond to accusations of slowing the game
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a 'slow game' against the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a ‘slow game’ against the All Blacks.

Peyper revealed that “not once” have the Springboks got feedback that they slow the game down in 2026 following the new protocols for feedback. The former referee who now consults to the Springboks confirmed the law that the Springboks play to, which is that they have 30 seconds from the time the mark is given to form the set piece.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Three-time Champions Cup winner joins coaching staff of Élite 1 hopefuls
Rugby.summary: Toulon legend Jocelino Suta has joined the coaching staff of Toulon ahead of the 2026/27 AXA Élite 1 Féminine season.
Rugby.body:
Toulon legend Jocelino Suta has joined the coaching staff of Rugby Club Toulon Provence Méditerranée ahead of the 2026/27 AXA Élite 1 Féminine season. Across a 13-year playing career the Vanuatu-born enforcer made 233 appearances for Toulon across a decade at the club, won three Champions Cup titles and earned six caps for France.

Suta came off the bench in the 2013 and 2014 Champions Cup Final successes against Clermont and Saracens, as a squad containing the likes of Jonny Wilkinson, Bakkies Botha, Matt Giteau and Carl Hayman dominated continental club rugby. In 2015, Suta made seven tournament appearances as the club claimed a third title in a row.

Newcastle Red Bulls lock Oscar Usher has signed a new three-year deal. The 22-year-old won the club's young player of the year award last season in his first full year as a professional.

"Creating opportunities for young local players is a massive part of what Newcastle Red Bulls are about, and Oscar has seized his chance by showing a tremendous work ethic and desire to improve," head coach Dan McFarland told the club website., external

Rugby.title: Wales centre James signs new Scarlets contract
Rugby.summary: Wales centre Eddie James signs a new contract with Scarlets before the start of the 2026-27 season.
Rugby.body:
Wales centre Eddie James has signed a new contract with Scarlets. After making his international debut in 2024, James became a Wales regular in the 2025-26 season under head coach Steve Tandy and now has 11 caps to his name.

The 24-year-old still had a year to run on his existing contract but has committed early to his home region. "Growing up in the region and supporting the Scarlets as a youngster, the club means a huge amount to me," said James.

Rugby.title: How the Springbok Women reacted after 'proper Test match' against Fiji
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September said it was "mission accomplished" for the team after their completed a Test series whitewash against the Fijiana XV.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September said it was “mission accomplished” for the team after their completed a Test series whitewash against the Fijiana XV. A week after South Africa had beaten Fiji 55-12 in Suva, the Boks battled their way to a 29-22 victory in Lautoka to wrap up the nation’s first-ever tour of Fiji with walkover success after two fixtures.

“We wanted a clean sweep, so that was mission accomplished,” September said. “We expected Fiji to come back stronger in the second test after winning 55-12 in the first and they did. This was a proper Test match.”

Rugby.title: Dual international Willis Halaholo announces retirement
Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Tonga centre Willis Halaholo has announced his retirement at the age of 36.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and Tonga centre Willis Halaholo has announced his retirement at the age of 36. The nine-cap Wales international made the announcement on social media on Monday, sharing a video in which he said he plans to move into coaching.

The Auckland-born centre made the move to Cardiff from the Hurricanes in 2016, and qualified to play for Wales in 2019. After initially being named in a Wales squad in 2019, an ACL injury meant he would have to wait until 2021 before he would play international rugby.

Rugby.title: Back-row pair parachuted into Red Roses training camp
Rugby.summary: Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has called Daisy Hibbert-Jones and Sophie McQueen into the team's University of Nottingham training camp.
Rugby.body:
Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has called Daisy Hibbert-Jones and Sophie McQueen into the team’s University of Nottingham training camp. The Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 are entering the third week of their WXV Global Series preparations. In September and October, England will play Canada three times, as well as the Black Ferns, Wallaroos and USA Women’s Eagles.

Hibbert-Jones, 23, earned one cap for England at WXV 1 in 2023 as the Red Roses claimed the inaugural title in New Zealand. Last season the back-row captained Loughborough Lightning in JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby to a sixth-place finish in the league.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks 2IC Neil Barnes isn't satisfied with his team's efforts to begin the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour, despite an accumulated 142-40 scoreline through three games against their club opponents.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks 2IC Neil Barnes isn’t satisfied with his team’s efforts to begin the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, despite an accumulated 142-40 scoreline through three games against their club opponents.

New Zealand handed the Bulls a 50-19 defeat at Loftus Versfeld over the weekend, putting up a more staunch fight in areas like their driving maul defence that hurt them a week earlier against the Stormers. The intervening Sharks game ended with a goose-egg for the hosts.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales and Cardiff centre Halaholo retires
Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Cardiff centre Willis Halaholo has ended his professional rugby career after 'a series of niggling injuries'.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and Cardiff centre Willis Halaholo has ended his professional rugby career. The 36-year-old announced his retirement on social media, saying "the mind is still keen to carry on but I think the body has had enough".

Auckland-born Halaholo qualified for Wales under residency rules and won the last of his nine Wales caps in April 2022. He went on to play three times for Tonga. He began his career in New Zealand with Southland before spells with both Waikato and Hurricanes, where he won a Super Rugby title.

Rugby.title: 'Try once': Aussie convert explains switch from Black Ferns ahead of Test
Rugby.summary: Despite Tapsell playing rugby in New Zealand since she was eight years old, the Western Force forward was born in Melbourne.
Rugby.body:
Pia Tapsell has no qualms about being in the Wallaroos squad, despite growing up in New Zealand and playing Test rugby for Australia’s bitter rivals. Tapsell became one of the few women’s international rugby union players to switch allegiances after she named in the Australian squad to face the Black Ferns in Auckland on Saturday.

It’s the first time the Wallaroos have experienced a player swap from a tier-one nation, although the Wallabies notably had prop Alex Hodgman play for the green and gold in 2024 after switching from the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: Rising star stays put in Australia after declining PNG Chiefs offer
Rugby.summary: Kadin and his brother Treyvon have been at the centre of contract speculation following their breakout seasons with the Brumbies and Queensland Reds respectively.
Rugby.body:
Kadin Pritchard admits it was an easy decision to re-sign with the ACT Brumbies and stay in rugby union until the end of 2030, despite receiving a sparkling offer to join PNG Chiefs.

Kadin and his brother Treyvon have been at the centre of contract speculation following their breakout seasons with the Brumbies and Queensland Reds respectively. They attracted headlines when the incoming NRL club approached the pair looking to poach them for their inaugural roster in 2028, which risked dealing a blow to Rugby Australia as they look primed for a future Wallabies debut.

Rugby.title: Regarding Henry: Why Australian rugby has a new centre of attention
Rugby.summary: Isaac Henry's display against Japan proved that other brands - other than Joseph-Aukuso Sua’ali’i - are available for the Wallabies' No.13 jersey.
Rugby.body:
The UK broadcasting rules are strict. When presenters on a telly show inadvertently mention a prominent commercial product on air, it is considered to be free advertising. The culprit is required to qualify the gaff with the prompt disclaimer ‘other brands are available, of course’. Usually, with a hint of a smirk curling around the corners of the mouth.

Rugby Australia could do with introducing a similar practice now. When Joseph-Aukuso Sua’ali’i was trumpeted as RA’s next big thing by ex-chairman Hamish McLennan at the end of 2023, the free advertising fanfare was as loud as the ‘musack’ filling the empty spaces in a South African rugby stadium:

Rugby.title: Steve Hansen: 'It doesn't matter' if Richie Mo'unga plays in South Africa
Rugby.summary: Sir Steve Hansen has weighed in on the All Blacks' decision to bring Richie Mo'unga into camp as a replacement for Billy Proctor, who has headed home after picking up a shoulder injury.
Rugby.body:
Sir Steve Hansen has weighed in on the All Blacks‘ decision to bring Richie Mo’unga into camp as a replacement for Billy Proctor, who has headed home after picking up a shoulder injury.

The ex-New Zealand head coach, who selected Mo’unga at No.10 during the 2019 Rugby World Cup, commended the current group, led by Dave Rennie, for not rushing the decision to find Proctor’s replacement, saying the time taken to assess their options builds confidence that they have made the right choice.

Rugby.title: The four top performers from round three of the Hilux NPC
Rugby.summary: The third round of the NPC saw some landmark records established and new contenders emerge.
Rugby.body:
The third round of the NPC saw some landmark records established and new contenders emerge. Hawke’s Bay stayed on top of the table with a 44-31 win over Auckland. Flanker Cooper Flanders from the 2019 Hastings Boys’ High School National Top Four-winning First XV has been a slow burn, but with two tries and 16 tackles, he has carried on his strong recent form and looks more settled and confident. Can he soar to the heights of his brother Devan Flanders?

Otago required late heroics from All Black Christian Lio-Willie and All Blacks XV winger Jona Nareki to quell Manawatu 29-27 after trailing 24-7. There was a similarly stoic comeback from Southland to upset Waikato 32-31 in Invercargill. In just his third appearance, 19-year-old Jimmy “The Boot” Taylor landed a sideline conversion with the last kick of the game to win it for the Stags.

Rugby.title: 'Mixed bag': Mike Blair delivers honest All Blacks attack assessment
Rugby.summary: Looking back, Blair was pleased with the overall performance against the Bulls, but also believed they could have been more clinical.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair has described his side’s attacking progress as a “mixed bag” to date, despite winning all six contests under Dave Rennie in 2026. Blair assumed the attack role at the start of the 2026 international season, joining the coaching staff of Rennie, Neil Barnes, Tana Umaga, and Jason Ryan.

The experienced Scotland halfback, speaking to media in Pretoria, was asked how he feels the attack is progressing after the three encounters against South African URC sides. Looking back, Blair was pleased with the overall performance against the Bulls, but also believed they could have been more clinical.

Rugby.title: 'That’s what the All Blacks don’t have': Ex-Bok coach highlights Dave Rennie's issue
Rugby.summary: Former Springboks head coach Heyneke Meyer believes that the gulf in depth between the two sides will be the difference in the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Former Springboks head coach Heyneke Meyer believes that the gulf in depth between the two sides will be the difference in the Greatest Rivalry series. According to the ex-coach the All Blacks don’t have the numbers in the forwards to match the Boks, while the game has changed to suit South Africa.

The eligibility rules in New Zealand have meant that a number of players head offshore when their international careers aren’t progressing, leading to a lot of departures in their late 20s.

Rugby.title: Predicted All Blacks' 23 to face the Springboks in the first Test
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks will name their team to face the Springboks on Thursday, with a number of players uncertain after injuries across the first three warm-up games.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks will name their team to face the Springboks on Thursday, with a number of players uncertain after injuries across the first three warm-up games. Prop Ollie Norris is the latest to be sent home after succumbing to an injury, while Cortez Ratima joins the uncertain list with a knee complaint.

Centre Billy Proctor, winger Caleb Clarke, hooker George Bell are all ruled out of further participation and have been sent home. In doubt includes Will Jordan (back complaint), Cam Roigard (hamstring), Damian McKenzie (ankle), and Ratima, with McKenzie the most worrying of the injuries according to head coach Dave Rennie.

Rugby.title: Report: Former Wallabies coach turned NRL assistant poised for Waratahs return
Rugby.summary: In 2025, Cheika led the Tigers to the Premiership final, before jetting back to Australia to help the Roosters in the NRL.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallabies head coach and current Sydney Roosters assistant coach Michael Cheika is set to make a return to the NSW Waratahs. According to the Sydney Morning Herald, Cheika will be announced as the club’s new head coach 12 years after clinching the club’s first Super Rugby title.

“According to informed sources speaking on the condition of anonymity, Cheika’s likely two-year deal is currently being finalised. The Waratahs are set to announce their new coach later this week,” the SMH reported.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga is back and desperate to make up for lost time
Rugby.summary: The return of RIchie Mo'unga has long been anticipated and he will soon get the chance to show Dave Rennie what he can do
Rugby.body:
A bit like the Mounties, it was always the case that Dave Rennie was going to get his man and bring Richie Mo’unga into the All Blacks. Everyone knew this was inevitable – that the All Blacks were almost certainly going to see someone suffer a tour-ending injury in South Africa and that Mo’unga would be deemed the right replacement by Rennie almost regardless of who was heading home.

As it turned out, it was midfielder Billy Proctor who cracked his shoulder in the opening game and Rennie was able to persuade the New Zealand Rugby board of directors that Mo’unga, a specialist No 10, was the player he needed to call-up.

Rugby.title: WRU statement: 'Highly personal insults and attacks' directed at staff
Rugby.summary: The WRU have decried what they have described as'highly personal insults and attacks' directed at their staff and members of the board in recent weeks.
Rugby.body:
The WRU have decried what they have described as’highly personal insults and attacks’ directed at their staff and members of the board in recent weeks. In what amounts to more of a open letter to the Welsh rugby public than a traditional statement, the WRU have asked fans to desist from attacks directed at their personal.

The statement reads: “Whatever your views about what is best for the future of Welsh rugby, there is no justification for the highly personal insults and attacks that have been recently directed at members of our staff and at the WRU Board.

Rugby.summary: Without knowing that was happening across the ditch, Wallaby Taniela Tupou did all front-rowers proud on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
TOWNSVILLE: New Zealand’s NPC celebrated ‘Front Row Round’ this week, recognising the hookers and props who have contributed to provincial rugby over 50 years. Without knowing that was happening across the ditch, Wallaby Taniela Tupou did all front-rowers proud on Saturday.

Tupou hadn’t scored in consecutive games since April 2021, when the world-renowned tighthead was suiting up for the Queensland Reds. The now 72-Test prop rewrote the script with a memorable double on Saturday, playing a leading role in a 56-17 win over Japan.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie opens up on All Blacks’ progress ahead of first SA Test
Rugby.summary: Stand-in All Blacks captain Codie Taylor, who scored a double in his first appearance on tour, said that he feels as though his side has made considerable strides during these tour outings.
Rugby.body:
Despite the All Blacks securing three wins from three games so far on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, head coach Dave Rennie is keeping his feet firmly on the ground. His side put 50 points on the 2026 United Rugby Championship runners-up, the Bulls, 54 on the Sharks, and 38 on the Stormers, charging to six wins on the trot ahead of the four-Test series.

But Rennie is clear that they are far from the perfect product, and will need a shift in quality if they want to secure a famous victory at Ellis Park next weekend. Touching on the contest post-match in Pretoria, the All Blacks head coach said the scoreline is a positive, but there were still aspects of the game that were “frustrating”.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks and Blues loose-forward Anton Segner has earned the man-of-the-match award against the Bulls in Pretoria, where Dave Rennie’s side overcame the 2026 URC runners-up, 50-19.

Segner, who made his All Blacks debut against Italy in Wellington, has ramped up pressure on the All Blacks selectors ahead of the first Test against the Springboks. The 25-year-old added twelve carries and thirteen tackles in his dominant performance, while his breakdown turnovers will also please Rennie and the coaching staff.

Rugby.summary: The All Blacks have beaten the Bulls by 50-19 in Pretoria to remain undefeated on the Greatest Rivalry tour.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have beaten the Bulls by 50-19 in Pretoria to remain undefeated on the Greatest Rivalry tour. Outstanding performances from Anton Segner, wingers Josh Moorby and Leroy Carter and Josh Jacomb fuelled a high-tempo All Blacks team that looked the sharpest it has so far on the tour.

The All Blacks survived an early onslaught from the home side, repelling multiple mauls from the five before a statement scrum which put the Bulls pack on the floor. After coming up inches short of the line, the Bulls were given a scrum five out which the All Blacks won a penalty against the feed.

Rugby.title: USA Rugby adopts T1 as official non-contact game ahead of home World Cups
Rugby.summary: USA Rugby and USA Youth & High School Rugby have formally adopted T1 Rugby as the official non-contact version of the game in the United States...
Rugby.body:
USA Rugby and USA Youth & High School Rugby have formally adopted T1 Rugby as the official non-contact version of the game in the United States, in a move designed to boost participation ahead of the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups on American soil in 2031 and 2033.

Developed by World Rugby and launched in 2023, T1 replaces tackling with touches or flags while retaining rugby’s core principles. Played seven-a-side on a half-pitch, the format is aimed at schools, clubs and youth organisations as an accessible entry point into the sport.

Rugby.summary: Ospreys are set to announce former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a new member of their board before the 2026-27 season.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones is poised to return to the Ospreys as a director. The 40-year-old is set to be announced as a board member by the Swansea-based club next week.

Jones made his Ospreys debut in 2005, a year after he broke through with Swansea RFC, and helped the club to three titles and an Anglo-Welsh Cup triumph. The former lock is to return at a turbulent time as the club fights for survival under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans to cut to three professional men's sides.

Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) states there is no prospect of the game generating enough revenue to fund four professional teams beyond 2028.
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has stated there is no realistic prospect of the game generating enough revenue to fund four professional teams in the country beyond 2028. The WRU's board has released a lengthy statement after former Wales captain Jonathan Davies called for them to step down.

There has been a concerted attempt to try to oust the WRU board this week. Businesswoman Hayley Parsons called for them to stand down before Davies' intervention, while former Principality Building Society chief operating officer Rob Regan has offered to oversee an interim board.

Rugby.body:
The second week of Alan Jones’s sexual misconduct trial has ended, as an ex-radio staffer alleges a power imbalance stopped him bringing forward claims earlier. A former radio station employee felt he could not tell anyone he was being indecently assaulted by Alan Jones because of the talkback titan’s extraordinary power and influence.

He is one of six men who allege Jones kissed, groped or subjected them to sexual misconduct between 2003 and 2020 across Sydney and the NSW Southern Highlands. The 85-year-old has pleaded not guilty to 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching without consent.

Rugby.body:
Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when the world's best young players compete at Dakar 2026 in Senegal. The tournament will kick off on November 1 at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, just one day after the opening ceremony on October 31. Medals will be awarded on November 2 and 3.

Dakar 2026 will make history as the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the African continent. The games will bring together around 2,700 young athletes competing across 25 different sports, including athletics, boxing, 3x3 basketball and coastal rowing.

Rugby.title: Rieko Ioane opens up on questioning whether his All Blacks career was over
Rugby.summary: Few All Blacks careers capture the hype, awe and contention of Rieko Ioane's. In July, a decade after becoming the eighth-youngest All Black ever in his 2016 debut, he was dropped from the squad for the first time
Rugby.body:
Few All Blacks careers capture the hype, awe and contention of Rieko Ioane’s. In July, a decade after becoming the eighth-youngest All Black ever in his 2016 debut, he was dropped from the squad for the first time. The now 29-year-old has since been recalled in an expanded squad for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, and has opened up on thinking his All Blacks days were done.

Sitting on 40 career Test tries, the eighth-most in All Blacks history, Ioane’s elite finishing was a constant feature of the team in his early years, although that strike rate dropped off considerably with his 2020 move to the midfield.

The now 29-year-old has since been recalled in an expanded squad for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, and has opened up on thinking his All Blacks days were done.

Sitting on 40 career Test tries, the eighth-most in All Blacks history, Ioane’s elite finishing was a constant feature of the team in his early years, although that strike rate dropped off considerably with his 2020 move to the midfield.

Rugby.title: All Blacks flyer becomes third South Africa tour casualty

Rugby.title: Davies calls for WRU board to step down
Rugby.summary: Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies calls for the Welsh Rugby Union board to step down.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies has called for the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) board to step down. Calls for the governing body's board to resign have come from Welsh business leaders while local Swansea politicians have demanded that chief executive Abi Tierney leave her role.

There are 11 members on the board following the departure of chair Richard Collier-Keywood in March 2026. Tierney is joined by interim vice-chair John Manders, independent directors Jamie Roberts, Jennifer Mathias, Andrew Williams, Alison Thorne and Amanda Bennett, elected members Claire Donovan, Chris Jones and Colin Wilks and interim Professional Rugby Board (PRB) chair Marianne Okland.

Rugby.title: Start of England's community rugby season postponed
Rugby.summary: The Rugby Football Union delays the start of the community rugby season because of concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions affecting much of England.
Rugby.body:
The Rugby Football Union has delayed the start of the community rugby season because of concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions affecting much of England. According to officials, 71.3% of England is now in drought while the country has recorded its driest July since records began in 1836.

In recent weeks, the RFU has reminded its members of existing guidance on managing rugby pitches in drought conditions and carrying out risk assessments to see if pitches are safe to use and to mitigate the risks of injury.

Rugby.summary: NBA superstar San Antonio Spurs forward-centre Victor Wembanyama has spent this week training with Pro D2 promotion hopefuls Provence Rugby at the Maurice-David Stadium.
Rugby.body:
NBA superstar San Antonio Spurs forward-centre Victor Wembanyama has spent this week training with Pro D2 promotion hopefuls Provence Rugby at the Maurice-David Stadium. Wembanyama, 22, who hails from Le Chesnay in the western suburbs of Paris, was the first pick in the 2023 NBA draft and is a two-time NBA All-Star, and spent the week taking part in several drills during on-field training sessions with Philippe Saint-André’s squad.

He was part of the France squad that won an Olympic silver medal at the Paris Games, but there is very little prospect of the 7 ft 4 in star ever switching codes after signing a five-year £186m extension with the Spurs last month.

Rugby.title: 57-cap prop returns to centrally contracted Ireland group for 2026/27
Rugby.summary: Experienced Ireland prop Linda Djougang has rejoined the union's centrally contracted programme for the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Experienced Ireland prop Linda Djougang has rejoined the union’s centrally contracted programme for the 2026/27 season. Last year the 57-cap front-row stepped away from the full-time programme to pursue her career outside of rugby, but remained a player of national interest and started all five Guinness Women’s Six Nations fixtures in 2026.

Sophie Barrett, Kate Jordan, Aoibheann McGrath and Eilís Cahill – who all made their Test debuts at this year’s Championship – have all earned their first national contracts. This centralised group of 31 players has been announced three months after Scott Bemand’s side enjoyed a record-breaking Women’s Six Nations campaign. This included a crowd of 31,294 at the team’s first standalone fixture at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: Shifting sands in the game
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks will play the Bulls who have, in coach Kennedy Tsimba, a visionary who has evolved the game in South Africa
Rugby.body:
In the Shona language native to Zimbabwe there is a well-known phrase: ‘tsimba itsoka’. It means ‘no foot, no footprint’ and it refers firstly to the footprint an animal may leave on the veld; on the larger scale of human activity, it highlights to the deep mark a man or a woman may leave on the ground of life.

A few weeks ago, I met Kennedy Tsimba, the current Skills coach of the Pretoria-based Bulls. As a player, Kennedy was a star in Sevens and he was anointed the ‘King of Bloemfontein’ for his record-breaking try-scoring feats with the Cheetahs. Tsimba became the fastest player to score over 1000 points in the Currie Cup, the Vodacom Cup and Super Rugby during his six-year stint in the Vrystaat and he is remembered. The footprint is strong.

Rugby.title: Ben Gunter’s remarkable journey from Brisbane groundskeeper to Japan star
Rugby.summary: In my five years at BBC, no First XV debut seemed to generate more anticipation than when Gunter first took the field as a 15-year-old.
Rugby.body:
Ben Gunter was two grades above me at Brisbane Boys’ College. In my five years at the school, no First XV debut seemed to generate more anticipation than when Gunter first took the field as a 15-year-old, starring alongside future Wallaby Isaac Henry that season.

It genuinely was the talk of Toowong that week, as a school of rugby-mad kids waited to see how a Year 10 prospect would fare against the best of the GPS. Gunter took the field draped in green, white and black, and quickly became an integral part of that side.

Rugby.title: New All Blacks Sevens coach reveals stance on XVs stars chasing Olympics
Rugby.summary: Willie Rickards played in eight tournaments for the All Blacks Sevens from 2006 to 2009. He succeeds Tomasi Cama.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks Sevens have a new head coach. Willie Rickards played in eight tournaments for the All Blacks Sevens from 2006 to 2009. He succeeds Tomasi Cama, who was involved with the 14-time SVNS Series champions for two decades and 150 tournaments as a player and coach.

Rickards represented Southland (28 games), Taranaki (19 games) and the Highlanders (2 games) as a player before moving into coaching. He led the Taranaki Sevens programme to a National Championship in 2013 and was NPC Skills Coach during the 2014 NPC Premiership-winning campaign. He then progressed to Assistant Coach and Head Coach (2018-2020). His tenure included a notable Ranfurly Shield win over Canterbury, 55-43 in Christchurch in 2017. However, the overall record as head coach was a modest 12 wins in 33 matches.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz: Fabrizio Romano breaks news US Open champion is to make comeback from wrist injury at Flushing Meadows
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz: Fabrizio Romano breaks news US Open champion is to make comeback from wrist injury at Flushing Meadows Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz will make his comeback from a wrist injury at the US Open as he seeks to defend his title at Flushing Meadows. The seven-time grand slam champion has not played on the ATP Tour since April, when he withdrew from the Barcelona Open with a wrist issue, with Alcaraz missing his defence of his French Open title and Wimbledon.

Alcaraz was due to return at the Cincinnati Open this month before withdrawing from that event, then enlisted the help of football transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano to announce his US Open comeback.

Tennis.title: US Open offers biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history
Tennis.summary: The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year.
Tennis.body:
The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year. The singles' champions will receive $5.5m (£4.03m) each in a 10% increase on 2025.

First-round losers will take home $140,000 (£102,667) - which is $30,000 and 27% more than last year. The prize pool includes a $2m (£1.47m) contribution to a welfare fund, which leading players have been demanding from all the Grand Slams.

Tennis.title: One month or four years? Timing key in Kyrgios ban
Tennis.summary: The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition.
Tennis.body:
The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition. The 2022 Wimbledon finalist tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine at June's grass court event in Mallorca, and is currently serving a mandatory provisional suspension.

The ban could theoretically stretch to four years, but it will be a maximum of three months if the Australian can satisfy investigators he took the drug out of competition. A player is deemed to be 'in competition' from the day the draws they are competing in begin until they leave the tournament after their final match.

Tennis.title: 'I feel I am imprisoning myself'
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic discusses being his own biggest doubter and the Belgrade childhood that shaped him in a new documentary.
Tennis.body:
Nobody doubts Novak Djokovic more than himself. Djokovic has won almost everything there is in tennis. No man has more Grand Slam singles titles or Masters 1,000 crowns than him. He will go down in history as one of the greatest players of all time, if not the greatest.

But even now, at the age of 39, that is not enough for the Serb. "I cannot say I feel content with what I have and who I am," he says in a new Amazon documentary. "I am always looking to be more - better, faster, stronger. Oftentimes I feel I am imprisoning myself."

Tennis.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bejlek as slump continues
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffer a setback in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek at the Cincinnati Open.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffered another blow as she crumbled in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek in the fourth round at the Cincinnati Open.

The Belarusian top seed was 5-1 up in a first-set tiebreak and 4-1 in front in the second set, but Czech Bejlek rallied back on both occasions to win 7-6 (9-7) 6-4. Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under threat, with Elena Rybakina - who faces Iga Swiatek in an eye-catching quarter-final on Thursday - able to replace her at the top of the rankings if she reaches the Cincinnati final.

Tennis.title: Why positive cocaine test could mean end of Kyrgios' career
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios once said he did not want to play tennis into his 30s. A positive cocaine test could have brought an end to his career aged 31.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s. But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.

In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility. But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.
