Britain's Arthur Fery was knocked out of the Cincinnati Open, but only after a thrilling fightback was halted by Alex de Minaur following several rain delays. In the end, fifth seed De Minaur ground out a 7-5 7-6 (7-3) win, but rain delays occurred before the contest, after the first game, following the end of the first set and with De Minaur 7-5 5-1 ahead, one game from the last-16 stage.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s Ex-Coach Sends Strongly-Worded Message to Defend Rafael Jodar After Cincinnati Open Controversy
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s Ex-Coach Sends Strongly-Worded Message to Defend Rafael Jodar After Cincinnati Open Controversy Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu's former coach, Mark Petchey, came to Rafael Jodar's defense on Sunday after the Spaniard found himself at the center of controversy during the Cincinnati Open. The controversy erupted during the third set of Jodar's second-round match against Denis Shapovalov on Saturday. The Spaniard fought back from a 1-5 deficit and saved match points to win 7-5, 4-6, 7-5. During the deciding set, he stopped play twice, claiming that he had broken his shoelaces. The second incident came while he was trailing 3-5, forcing a lengthy pause as he completely changed his shoes.

Shapovalov grew visibly frustrated and complained to the chair umpire. He accused Jodar of using the shoelace delays not only to fix his equipment but also to disrupt his rhythm, get some rest, and drink water. The 19-year-old also faced backlash online, as he reportedly used similar tactics during his matches against Taylor Fritz at the Mubadala DC Open and Brandon Nakashima at the Canadian Open.

Tennis.title: Could Raducanu Retire Suddenly? Andrew Castle Says It Wouldn't Surprise Him
Tennis.summary: Could Raducanu Retire Suddenly? Andrew Castle Says It Wouldn't Surprise Him TennisTemple
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu is still sidelined after a stress fracture in her right leg, which notably forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon. The 2021 US Open champion is also expected to miss the North American hard-court swing after pulling out of the US Open. She was also not selected for the Billie Jean King Cup final with Great Britain at the end of September.

Faced with this succession of physical problems, former British player Andrew Castle believes that a radical decision from Raducanu would not be totally surprising. "Well, let's put it this way. I have absolutely no information about what's going on in her circle, but it wouldn't surprise me if one day, without warning, she simply says: 'I've had enough of all this.' After all, don't we all say that? She has no one to answer to but herself and her family. That's it. Sponsors and the people around her are not the ones driving this career. It's her choice, but I hope she continues," the former British tennis player told Betway.

The 2021 US Open champion is also expected to miss the North American hard-court swing after pulling out of the US Open. She was also not selected for the Billie Jean King Cup final with Great Britain at the end of September.

Faced with this succession of physical problems, former British player Andrew Castle believes that a radical decision from Raducanu would not be totally surprising. "Well, let's put it this way. I have absolutely no information about what's going on in her circle, but it wouldn't surprise me if one day, without warning, she simply says: 'I've had enough of all this.' After all, don't we all say that? She has no one to answer to but herself and her family. That's it. Sponsors and the people around her are not the ones driving this career. It's her choice, but I hope she continues," the former British tennis player told Betway.

The 39-year-old said the condition was exacerbated by the heat and humidity in Ohio as he visibly struggled in a 6-2 4-6 4-6 loss to Argentina's world No 50 Thiago Agustin Tirante.

Djokovic, currently world No 5 and playing his first match since losing to Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon semi-finals in July, slumped to his hands and knees before taking a medical timeout midway through the second set.

Tennis.body:
Former British World No. 1 Andrew Castle recently made a bold prediction about Emma Raducanu's career as she continues to recover from injury. Raducanu was last seen in action at the HSBC Championships, where she enjoyed a strong run and reached the final. She has also pulled out of the Canadian Open and the US Open as she continues her recovery. The US Open is scheduled to take place from August 23 to September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

Tennis.title: Fery wins on return as Djokovic struggles in heat
Tennis.summary: Britain's Arthur Fery beats Australia's James Duckworth at the Cincinnati Open but Novak Djokovic falls to a shock defeat by Argentina's Thiago Tirante.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Arthur Fery beat Australia's James Duckworth at the Cincinnati Open, in his first match since making a shock run to the Wimbledon semi-finals last month. Fery, who jumped to a career-high world ranking of 36 following his Wimbledon success, won 6-4 2-6 7-6 (7-4) in two hours and 34 minutes against Duckworth in Ohio as he warms up for the US Open later this month.

The 24-year-old was given a wildcard into his home Grand Slam, having been ranked 114th in the world before the start of the tournament and having never been beyond the second round of a Grand Slam, and defied all expectations to reach the semi-finals where he lost to Alexander Zverev.

Tennis.summary: Why I think Jack Draper should now skip the US Open after his first round loss at the Cincinnati Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper lost again last night, meaning that of the last five tournaments he has entered, spanning five months, he has suffered four first-round exits. This is not nearly at the level we expect from the former world number four, but such a downturn is through no fault of his own.

Instead, this has been the cruel result of an injury he simply cannot fix, no matter what he tries. Rest has not resolved the bone bruising in his arm, and surgery would only make things worse. It’s the worst place for a professional athlete to be in, and it comes at a crucial time in Jack Draper’s career, just when he seemed set to be a mainstay at the apex for years to come.

Golf.title: The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms
Golf.summary: I wrote my first book, “The Green Road Home," 40 years ago. I didn’t know what I was doing, either as a caddie or writer, but I soaked it up. The post The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I was 25 when I wrote “The Green Road Home,” in my parents’ house in Patchogue, on the South Shore of Long Island. On my 26th birthday a copy of it arrived there, hot off the press. That was in 1986. This piece is from a new afterword for it, a 40th anniversary edition that was published recently.

I was kind of amazed, the day that first copy showed up 40 years ago, as I didn’t know what I was doing, certainly not as a caddie, but not as a writer, either, not really. Since then, not much has changed. I’ve come to accept that as a writer and reporter my thing is to puzzle on through. For better or for worse, that’s my modus operandi, the swing thought of my professional life. Ask questions, look around, size things up, like a detective. (TV’s Lieutenant Columbo is one of my inspirations.) I don’t know what could be more fun than being a reporter.

Golf.title: McIlroy and Scheffler suffer reversal of fortunes
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy says a bit of "good work" with his team helped him rediscover his form and take the lead in the first round of the BMW Championship.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler had a reversal of fortunes that few could have predicted on Thursday's opening day of the BMW Championship in St Louis. Reigning Masters champion McIlroy, who finished 66th out of 70 at last week's St Jude Championship, was one of five players to post a six-under-par 64 at Bellerive Country Club to take the joint lead.

But world number one Scheffler, who last Sunday won the first of the PGA Tour's three no cut end-of season play-off events by eight shots, opened with a two-over-par 72. The American, who had only recorded an over par score once in his past 18 rounds, finished one shot above the worst score of the opening round and joint 44th in the 50-man field.

Golf.body:
Royal Mayfair Golf Club, by all accounts, deserves its first word — royal. There’s its history — it’s been around for 104 years. There’s its location — it’s in the heart of Edmonton, Alberta. There’s its golf — it’s tree-laden course has hosted men’s and women’s professional events, including this week’s LPGA stop, the CPKC Women’s Open.

Nelly Korda can certify its standing. The world’s top-ranked player said she’s found good coffee shops and restaurants. She said she’s been enjoying her time on the golf course. She’s also just been looking around. “The golf course is beautiful,” she said. “I mean, you kind of have the skyline of kind of downtown Edmonton, too, on the golf course, which is really pretty.”

Golf.title: 7 musts for becoming a better putter, according to a top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tom Stickney shares six keys to focus on to perform better on the greens and reduce three-putts. The post 7 musts for becoming a better putter, according to a top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Putting can be mistakenly considered the simplest part of golf. The stroke is short, and there is no need to generate tremendous clubhead speed. Easy, right? As any avid golfer knows, that’s hardly the case. Although the stroke is small, putting is one of the most demanding skills in the game because small changes in alignment, balance, face angle or speed can produce dramatically different results. The margin for error is incredibly slim.

That’s why the key to becoming a better putter boils down to understanding a few fundamental principles and learning to repeat them under pressure. Check out below for a rundown of some of these key fundamentals and how they work together to create a solid stroke.

Golf.summary: Sun Mountain released the ClubGlider3 earlier this summer and our gear editor has some thoughts after taking it for few trips. The post Sun Mountain took my favorite travel bag and made it even better appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I will never travel with golf clubs in any other travel bag than the Sun Mountain ClubGlider. Full stop. Flying on American Airlines out of my former home airport in Philadelphia meant a better-than-not chance you would leave from one terminal (A, B, C or F) and return to any of the other three. If you parked in the garages, that means a long walk back to the car.

The ClubGlider’s extendable legs make lugging the golf bag from car to terminal and vice versa a breeze. It’s truly life-changing, not having to hold the weight of your clubs when moving from place to place.

Golf.body:
As Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy are battling for big bucks at this week’s 2026 BMW Championship, LIV Golf’s season finale is going down in Indianapolis after the original finale was canceled. The upstart league’s future is in serious doubt, and some of its players are readying escape plans.

Whether or not LIV’s biggest remaining stars — like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm — will be allowed to return to the PGA Tour is an open question. McIlroy provided an unforgiving opinion on the matter during his Wednesday press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship. McIlroy implied that the PGA Tour didn’t need LIV’s stars to come back. He did, though, admit that he expected them to return “eventually,” but that it would (and should) be a “tough, tough road back.”

Golf.title: 'If someone is willing to pay': Rory McIlroy defends skyrocketing prize money
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy, during his 2026 BMW Championship press conference, shot down the idea that there is too much money in pro golf. The post ‘If someone is willing to pay’: Rory McIlroy defends skyrocketing prize money appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy was on fire in his press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship, even by normal Rory McIlroy standards. Never one to hide his true feelings from reporters, the World No. 2 continued that tradition at Bellerive Country Club on Wednesday.

First, he dumped cold water on the idea that returning LIV Golf stars could improve the PGA Tour, burning them with one line: “Have they brought value to LIV?” Then, he quieted any suggestion that he should win Player of the Year honors, handed Scottie Scheffler the title early and suggested that if Scheffler kept putting as well as he did last week, McIlroy and the rest of the Tour’s stars are “F’d.”

Golf.title: How a course's unusual act of kindness resulted in a teen caddie's $125,000 tip

Golf.body:
LATER THIS WEEK, the students of greater Aiken, S.C., will return to school, and the weekday caddie yard at Old Barnwell will empty. Across enormous green fairways and inside bunkers shaped like dinosaur bones, it is usually not hard to find the teens of Aiken at Old Barnwell. They lumber around the golf course like percussionists in a folk rock band — their steps thumping against the hardened earth and their bags clanking with the sweet symphony of iron against iron.

Happen upon a game at Old Barnwell and you’ll quickly realize that it is not like other private golf clubs. Happen upon a conversation with one of Old Barnwell’s caddies and you’ll find out why.

Golf.title: 'Have they brought value to LIV?' Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees
Golf.summary: Should certain LIV Golf players be let back onto the PGA Tour? At the Tour’s BMW Championship, Rory McIlroy questioned their “value.” The post ‘Have they brought value to LIV?’ Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy, when asked whether certain LIV Golf players should be allowed back onto the PGA Tour, started his 22-word answer on Wednesday with a question of his own. The six-time major winner spoke one day before the Tour’s BMW Championship — and at about the same time as LIV CEO Scott O’Neil addressed the future of his league as it attempts to regroup after the loss of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. The exit has led to speculation on whether LIV players would stick with the league after its season-ending event this week, or look into avenues to play on the Tour, the circuit in which most of the pros had once played.

But McIlroy questioned the point of certain LIV pros returning. “I mean, I’d argue, have they brought value to LIV? You know?” he said. “I think the PGA Tour’s in a really good spot.”

Golf.title: Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it's not a fair fight
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler’s pursuit of Tiger Woods' career-earnings haul is a hot topic this week. But the chase needs to be kept in perspective. The post Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it’s not a fair fight appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Scottie Scheffler tells you he’s a rich man, he’s not talking about his bank account. He’s referring to his family: high-school-sweetheart-turned-wife Meredith and their towheaded sons, Bennett (2) and Remy (5 months). He’s referring to his faith (he’s a devout Christian and regular at Park Cities Presbyterian Church in Dallas). And, in a distant third among his soul-fillers, he’s referring to his golf (though not in the name of chasing titles or history or fame; Scheffler is driven by the singular pursuit of executing each shot and each task as it comes — with as much care, skill and focus as his body and mind will allow).

None of which to say that the guy hasn’t also banked a Brink’s truck or two full of cash. Scheffler’s career windfall has come into focus this week as he prepares for the second of three legs of the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup playoffs, the BMW Championship, because he is on the cusp of a seemingly momentous achievement: usurping Tiger Woods as the Tour’s all-time leading money earner. Scheffler ($119,964,411) trails Woods ($120,999,166) by “only” $1,034,755, meaning if he finishes in a three-way tie for third or better at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis, Scheffler will assume the gilded throne. After Scheffler’s exemplary form in Memphis last week, where he won by a touchdown and a two-point conversion, smart money says Woods’ record will fall this week.

Golf.title: 8 things LIV’s CEO told reporters at season finale — and what they mean

Golf.body:
WESTFIELD, Ind. — For the second time in two weeks and perhaps the last time in quite a while, LIV CEO Scott O’Neil sat in front of cameras and reporters (and many interested LIV staffers) for a proper, professional press conference.

It lasted 33 minutes. It was nearly 4,000 words long. And there were some clues into LIV’s present and its future, among plenty of veiled coach-speak, CEO-speak, leader-speak. I’m here to parse through it on your behalf, like Trent Crimm of the Independent, aka the fictitious reporter from “Ted Lasso” — whom O’Neil himself likened me to during the proceedings.

Golf.title: 'Tough road back' to PGA Tour from LIV
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy feels it could be a "tough road back" to the PGA Tour for those players currently signed up to LIV Golf.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy feels it could be a "tough road back" to the PGA Tour for those currently with LIV Golf. After Saudi Arabia confirmed it was withdrawing financial backing to the breakaway league in April, uncertainty surrounding its future has increased with next week's Team Championship cancelled.

That has left this week's event in Indianapolis as LIV's season finale. In January, five-time Major winner Brooks Koepka rejoined the PGA Tour under a deal that saw him forfeit any player equity shares for the next five years, while he is also ineligible for the $100m (£73.4m) FedEx Cup bonus scheme this year and had to make a $5m (£3.6m) donation to charity.

Golf.title: Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion Jack Whaley revisited the crucial shots from his winning week. The post Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Like the U.S. Open, hopefuls must first qualify to gain entry into the tournament, either by their WAGR ranking or by going through local and final qualifying. Once there, 36 holes of stroke play determine which 64 of the 312 players in the field will move on to the match-play portion of the championship. This year, 16 players battled for the 11 remaining match-play spots at the end of the stroke-play portion of the championship.

Among those 11 players who got through was Jack Whaley, who became the newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion shortly thereafter. After punching his ticket to the Round of 64, Whaley had to defeat six consecutive opponents in order to claim the title.

Golf.summary: GOLF contributor Shaun Tolson's recent trip to Virginia proved that the golf-rich state is indeed for lovers — food lovers, that is. The post From bison ribeyes to melon gazpacho, these are Virginia’s can’t-miss bites appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As a writer who traverses the globe covering golf, travel and all things food and beverage — and who racked up 110,000 frequent-flyer miles in 2025 — GOLF contributor Shaun Tolson has visited some of the world’s most famous golf clubs, resorts and best-kept secrets. Below, in Clubhouse Eats, he shares some of his favorite bites and sips from his recent travels.

It’s been more than 50 years since the advertising firm The Martin Agency (then Martin & Woltz Inc.) created the famous slogan “Virginia is for Lovers.” At the time, the slogan’s intention was to attract younger travelers to the state’s beaches, historical sites, and areas for outdoor adventure. But based on a few of my recent visits to Old Dominion — as the state is sometimes called — it’s clear Virginia is for food lovers, too.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy just hit LIV Golf with a brutal parting shot
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy just hit LIV Golf with a brutal parting shot Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Despite reports last week that LIV Golf had secured an angel investor for 2027, the league’s slow-motion collpase has continued unabated. The season-ending team championship was finally canceled, reports of countless unpaid vendors and employees began to surface, and persistent, albeit unsubstantiated, rumors that Jon Rahm’s LIV days were numbered continued to swirl. What happens next is anyone’s guess, but one thing is clear:

LIV Golf, as it has existed the past five years, is dead. It's said that you're not supposed to beat a dead horse, but after his pro-am appearance on Wednesday at the BMW Championship, Rory McIlroy—long one of LIV Golf's most outspoken critics—hit the floundering league with one last roundhouse for the road. Take it away, Rors.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's long odyssey is the product of what makes him great
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland's search for the best version of himself is ongoing. It's the product of a double-edge sword that he must learn to manage. The post Viktor Hovland’s long odyssey is the product of what makes him great appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Viktor Hovland is curious. It has been both a blessing and a curse for the Norwegian star, and it’s what will eventually deliver him to what he has been searching for. Back in 2023, Viktor Hovland was one of the four best players in the world. He posted top 10s at the Players, the Masters and the PGA Championship before winning the Memorial, BMW and Tour Championship. It was the type of ascension Hovland had been destined to make ever since he turned pro in June of 2019. Everything pointed to Viktor Hovland continuing his rise, stacking wins and adding major championships to his resume. But Viktor Hovland is curious; he’s a dreamer and a wanderer and a tinkerer. So he decided to pick at his swing. Nitpicks became coaching changes and Viktor Hovland marched off on a path all his own making.

One he’s still trying to come back from. “Now, especially looking back, I would say that it was more I was content with my game up until — my whole career up until 2023 in terms of my ball striking,” Hovland said on Tuesday ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship. “But it was always trying to nitpick and trying to find places where I can improve. Now, with kind of the struggles that I’ve had the last, I would say, three years, where my ball striking has just been drastically worse, you know, you take a little bit for granted how good it was before.”

Golf.title: LIV Golf captains confirm first DP World Tour starts in more than three years
Golf.summary: LIV Golf captains confirm first DP World Tour starts in more than three years Golfmagic
Golf.body:
European Ryder Cup legends Ian Poulter and Lee Westwood are set to make their returns to the DP World Tour (DPWT) later this year. The pair were among the first wave of players to be recruited by the LIV Golf League when it launched in June 2022.

Both golfers played in the opening tournament at Centurion Club and were subsequently hit with £100,000 fines for teeing it up without obtaining releases. They took the DPWT to a sports arbitration panel over the issue, but handed in their memberships after a panel of former high court judges ruled in favour of the Wentworth-based organisation in July 2023.

Golf.title: LIV Golf pro: Battle for survival "taking its toll" on CEO Scott O'Neil
Golf.summary: LIV Golf pro: Battle for survival "taking its toll" on CEO Scott O'Neil Golfmagic
Golf.body:
LIV Golf's battle for survival is taking a toll on the league's chief executive Scott O'Neil, according to Charles Howell III. O'Neil announced two weeks ago that LIV Golf had secured an unnamed lead investor to keep the competition running in 2027 after the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian financial backing.

The former NBA executive said a signed agreement was in place and had been approved by LIV's board, with the transaction expected to be finalised next month. LIV Golf's entire roster attended a meeting with the proposed new investor - understood to be the London-based private equity firm BC Partners - on Tuesday afternoon ahead of their season finale in Indianapolis.

Golf.title: LIV Golf slash prize money as players still ‘awaiting payments’ from last event - todays-golfer.com
Golf.summary: LIV Golf slash prize money as players still ‘awaiting payments’ from last event todays-golfer.com
Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s season will end in Indianapolis this week – and the prize money payout for players has changed dramatically. LIV Golf has slashed expected payouts for the end of the creaking league’s season after the cancellation of the Team Championships in Michigan.

The final LIV event of the 2026 season will take place this week in Indianapolis, with the team finale now folded into the individual stroke play tournament at Chatham Hills. In normal regular individual events, LIV distributes $20million for its 57 players, with the winner banking a $4m cheque. But this week, the individual purse will be set at $10.1million, with the champion earning just over $2million. As was confirmed at the start of the season, the top three players in the individual standings will share a bonus of $10million.

Golf.body:
There are golfers, Lee Trevino says, who think they can “really” play golf. And some may be right. “There’s a bunch of them out there that think they can really play golf,” Trevino said. “When you’re an amateur, you’re an amateur. When you’re messing with the pros, you’re messing with the pros. It’s like boxing. You know, if you fought Golden Gloves, that’s everyone you ever fought, and now you’re going to fight a professional that’s been in the ring for 10 years, you’re going to get killed. Eventually, you’ll get killed.

“So it’s the same thing in golf. You might bite a little bit. You might get a crumb here and there every once in a while.” The question is, how can you tell if someone is a player — or a non-player? On a recent episode of the Vanity Index Podcast — which you can listen to in full here — the ever-popular Trevino said he has his methods.

Golf.title: Instantly balance your setup with this clever practice hack
Golf.summary: If you’re someone who struggles with balance in your golf swing, this alignment-rod drill can get you on track. The post Instantly balance your setup with this clever practice hack appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Having balanced posture at address is a crucial component for solid and consistent ball striking. Watch Adam Scott’s swing. He starts from the same athletic, balanced position every time he puts a move on the ball. His consistent ball striking is thanks in large part to this attention to detail in his setup.

I recently saw GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero for a lesson, and the first thing he and his team noted was that my setup position was out of balance. With the aid of Swing Catalyst force plates, he noted that my weight was sitting too far in my heels at address, which led to issues in my swing.

Golf.title: Want to become a better ball striker? Start by improving these 4 things
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero explains the four things he focuses on to help students hit the ball better without a swing overhaul. The post Want to become a better ball striker? Start by improving these 4 things appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I recently made it down to Key West, Fla., for a “working escape” with my good friend Wade Hamilton, the director of golf at Montgomery Country Club (and a great teacher in his own right). We spent an afternoon at Key West Golf Club with student Sam Steele, who was looking to make better contact with his irons. He wasn’t interested in a new golf swing, just in a way to find the center of the face more often so the ball would start doing what he wanted.

The good news is that he didn’t need a rebuild. He just needed four small adjustments to click into place, and once they did, Sam left with more than solid strikes. He left with an actual plan, which is usually the difference between a player who improves and one who just keeps hitting range balls at random. We worked through it with a handful of feels and drills built around those four fixes. You can see the whole session in the latest episode of our Pro Work series below.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Indianapolis 2026 prize money: Winner's payout slashed in half at season finale
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Indianapolis 2026 prize money: Winner's payout slashed in half at season finale Golfmagic
Golf.body:
The LIV Golf Indianapolis champion is set to collect a significantly smaller cheque than winners have become accustomed to on the breakaway circuit. The individual purse for this week's 57-man event at The Club at Chatham Hills stands at $10.1 million, with the winner receiving $2.02 million.

That represents a substantial reduction from the $20m individual purses used at previous LIV Golf events, where first place traditionally carried a $4m prize. The change means the Indianapolis champion will receive almost exactly half the winner's payout that had become standard across LIV's individual tournaments.

Golf.title: My kids rejected golf. Would this backyard game have helped? | I tried it
Golf.summary: BucketGolf is a portable kit designed to make "golf a game that anyone can play." How well does it live up to that promise? The post My kids rejected golf. Would this backyard game have helped? | I tried it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As a father who tried — and failed — to get his son and daughter into golf, I sometimes wander down What If Lane. What if we’d lived closer to a municipal course with a robust junior program? What if I’d joined a fancy country club that offered golf camps for kids? What if, instead of mobiles, I’d installed range finders in their cribs?

In short, was there anything I could have done differently to inspire my progeny to take up the game? The list of hypotheticals is long, and to it I will now add another: what if I’d introduced them to BucketGolf?

Golf.title: Production Company Sues LIV for $1.2M in Missed Payments
Golf.summary: Production Company Sues LIV for $1.2M in Missed Payments Front Office Sports
Golf.body:
As LIV Golf’s rocky 2026 season concludes this week, one of the league’s still-unresolved financial disputes dates back to before the season even began. Fresh Tape Media, the company that produced and operated the league’s preseason media days event in January, is suing LIV for more than $1.23 million in missed payments and interest, according to a complaint filed in the Supreme Court of the State of New York on July 21. Due to the nature of the lawsuit, LIV was formally notified of the complaint only on Monday—the same day it officially announced the cancellation of its $40 million team championship that was scheduled for next week in Michigan.

It’s the latest company to go public with claims of missed payments from LIV, as various vendors and contractors have told Front Office Sports they are also owed money by the league. Mobii Systems Group Limited, a former technology partner of LIV, also sued the league last month for more than $1.1 million for breach of contract, unpaid invoices, and interest.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: When measuring a club-length, is it legal to leave the headcover on?
Golf.summary: If you are measuring club-lengths for relief, is it permissible to keep your club's headcover on? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: When measuring a club-length, is it legal to leave the headcover on? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. During the Masters, Sam Burns took a penalty drop from Rae’s Creek. He measured two club-lengths from the agreed point of entry with his driver…but left the headcover on! He did the same playing with Matthew Fitzpatrick when Fitzpatrick won the U.S. Open. Is this legitimate? – Alan Absolon, via email

That depends — was the headcover a cute one? Like, in the shape of an animal, or with a pom-pom? We kid. As long as the ball ends up in the right spot, the Rules don’t really care how you measure. Unless a player is trying to use the extra length of the headcover and drops at the very end of the two club-lengths-plus-headcover, it doesn’t matter in the least whether the headcover stays on or not.

Golf.title: 'Didn't do a ton': Rory McIlroy makes surprising admission after ugly playoff start
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy struggled mightily in last week's FedEx Cup playoffs opener, then he made a surprising admission about his preparation. The post ‘Didn’t do a ton’: Rory McIlroy makes surprising admission after ugly playoff start appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy played the weekend at last week’s FedEx St. Jude Championship. But that’s only because the limited-field event didn’t feature a cut. The five-time major champion struggled through four rough rounds at TPC Southwind, eventually finishing third-to-last among the players who didn’t withdraw from the event.

Then, when the bogeys were finally done for the week, McIlroy met with reporters and made a surprising admission: he didn’t really practice ahead of the first FedEx Cup playoff event.

Golf.title: Whaley earns Walker Cup spot after US Amateur win
Golf.summary: Jack Whaley is named in the 10‑man GB&I Walker Cup squad two days after winning the US Amateur Championship.
Golf.body:
Jack Whaley has been included in the Great Britain and Ireland team for the Walker Cup, two days after winning the US Amateur Championship. Whaley became just the third Englishman to lift the trophy since 1911 as he beat beat American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 in the final at Merion, Pennsylvania on Sunday.

The 22‑year‑old is one of four players included in the GB&I squad for the first time, alongside Ben Bolton, Sam Easterbrook and Josh Hill. Luke Poulter, son of Ryder Cup player Ian Poulter, is also in the 10-man squad for a second successive time after an impressive season with the University of Florida.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau announces surprise tour return - todays-golfer.com
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau announces surprise tour return todays-golfer.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has revealed he will be making a return to the DP World Tour this winter. The two-times US Open winner has not appeared on the circuit since 2022 and DeChambeau’s schedule for the 2027 season remains up in the air because of the ongoing uncertainty around LIV Golf.

DeChambeau has led the fight for LIV’s survival since it emerged the Saudi Public Investment Fund would be withdrawing its support at the end of the season. Ahead of his final LIV start of the season at Indianapolis, DeChambeau announced in a video with Gary Player that he would be teeing it up in this December’s Nedbank Golf Challenge. It will be DeChambeau’s second start in South Africa this year after he won on LIV’s inaugural visit in March.

Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler won his second tournament of the year, the FedEx St. Jude, in a pair of Nike Victory Pro 4 golf shoes. Shop them here. The post Scottie Scheffler’s athletic Nike golf shoes suit his powerful swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If sporting an athletic look is the on-course vibe that appeals most to you, Nike is likely a familiar brand in your closet. A decade after exiting the ball, club and bag side of the golf business, the Swoosh has remained synonymous with some of the game’s biggest names, partnering with World Nos. 1 and 2, Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy on the men’s side, and Nelly Korda and Michelle Wie West on the women’s side.

While we recreational players can’t necessarily ensure the same result as the pros when we try to replicate their equipment specs, we can certainly strive emulate their look as closely as possible by seeking out the apparel and footwear we see them wearing on Tour. And after Scheffler’s impressive performance at the FedEx St. Jude, we’re shining the spotlight on his Nike Victory Pro 4 spiked golf shoes, which you can buy at PGA TOUR Superstore.

Golf.title: Emotional Whaley credits dad for US Amateur glory
Golf.summary: It was very much a family affair for Jack Whaley as he became only the third Englishman to triumph in the US Amateur Championship on Sunday.
Golf.body:
It was very much a family affair for Jack Whaley as he became only the third Englishman to triumph in the US Amateur Championship on Sunday. The 22-year-old from Doncaster had his dad Andy caddying for him as he beat American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 in the final.

As a result, Whaley earned a place in the fields for the Masters, US Open and The Open at St Andrews in 2027, and an automatic berth in the Great Britain & Ireland Walker Cup team that will take on the United States at Lahinch in Ireland on 5 and 6 September.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Vendors Go Unpaid
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Vendors Go Unpaid Front Office Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf might be preparing for its next chapter with new investors, but more contractors and vendors claim they’re owed money by the league. The credit division of private investment firm BC Partners is exploring a funding deal with LIV to help the league continue operating in 2027 and beyond. This week’s LIV Golf Indianapolis event is set to pay out $30 million in prize money, and on Monday afternoon LIV Golf announced its season-ending $40 million team championship in Michigan next week is canceled.

As the tumultuous 2026 season comes to a close, no full-time employees are known to have seen any missed paychecks since the Saudi Public Investment Fund announced in April it would no longer fund LIV after this season.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf's season-ending tournament in Michigan cancelled RTE.ie
Golf.body:
LIV Golf's season-ending Team Championship tournament in Michigan has been cancelled to allow "full resources" to be used to put plans in place for the 2027 calendar. A statement by the breakaway league on Monday night confirmed the final event of this season’s schedule at The Cardinal at Saint John’s course had been scrapped.

This week’s Indianapolis 2026 Championships at Chatham Hills will instead conclude action for this year before LIV Golf will undergo major changes following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia Public Invest Fund as the key financial backer of the league.

Golf.title: LIV cancels final event to focus on 'next chapter'
Golf.summary: LIV Golf cancels its Team Championships in Michigan after weeks of speculation, saying it needs to focus on "building its next chapter".
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has cancelled its Team Championships in Michigan after weeks of speculation, saying it needs to focus on "building its next chapter". It had been widely expected that the event from 27 to 30 August would not happen, as players including Tyrrell Hatton entered the British Masters over the same dates and tickets were no longer being sold.

However, confirmation came on Monday with a statement from LIV Golf outlining changes to the schedule, meaning this week's event in Indianapolis will be the last of the season and double up as a team competition.

Golf.title: LIV Golf to Crown Season's Individual and Team Winners This Week in the City of Champions at LIV Golf Indianapolis 2026
Golf.summary: LIV Golf to Crown Season's Individual and Team Winners This Week in the City of Champions at LIV Golf Indianapolis 2026 LIV Golf
Golf.body:
The Club at Chatham Hills to host LIV Golf's 2026 finale Aug. 20-23 when the League will crown its Indianapolis Individual Tournament Champion, 2026 Season Individual Champion, and 2026 Team Champion in four-day stroke play competition

WESTFIELD, Ind. – LIV Golf, the global golf league blending world-class competition with entertainment and culture to grow the game worldwide, today confirmed that the League's 2026 season finale will celebrate an Indianapolis Champion, the 2026 Season Individual Champion and top three finishers and the 2026 Team Champion at the LIV Golf Indianapolis 2026 Championships. The four-day stroke play event will take place Aug. 20-23 at The Club at Chatham Hills where 57 players will contend for the Indianapolis individual title and final spots in the League's individual season long standings. The team competition will count the scores of all four players on each team every day, culminating with one of the 13 teams being crowned the 2026 LIV Golf Team Champion.

Golf.title: Canceled finale? Concerts in doubt? Inside LIV Golf's uncertain finishing stretch
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's final events will not go off as originally planned, something the league has purposely been keeping quiet. The post Canceled finale? Concerts in doubt? Inside LIV Golf’s uncertain finishing stretch appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s 2026 season will end this week, even if LIV hasn’t acknowledged as much. For weeks, golf fans have heard whispers of the league’s shortened season via reports from various outlets, but LIV’s official channels haven’t addressed the matter, leaving interested parties, including ticket-holders, in the dark.

As of early Monday afternoon, 10 days before the would-be first round of LIV’s team championship in Michigan, the league’s website still had the tournament, slated for The Cardinal at St. John’s, listed as an “upcoming event.” The site included links to “Get Tickets,” but when users accessed it, they received a notification that read “the tickets you were looking for are no longer available…”

Golf.title: 'When is this going to stop?': Scottie Scheffler fights off horrible break to win St. Jude

Golf.body:
Scottie Scheffler finally captured his second win of the season on Sunday at the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship. In the process, the World No. 1 ended a winless drought that stretched back to January.

While that would hardly be news for almost any other player, Scheffler is the best in the world and has repeatedly experienced near-misses all year long. But it all almost came undone when Scheffler suffered a horrendous break on the 3rd hole of the final round that threatened his lead as well as his comeback win and left the four-time major winner beside himself.

Golf.summary: In the latest Tour Confidential, GOLF’s writers discuss Jon Rahm's LIV Golf future, lessons from the U.S. Amateur and more. The post Tour Confidential: Jon Rahm’s LIV future, U.S. Amateur lessons and Scottie’s big win appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Check in every week for the unfiltered opinions of our writers and editors as they break down the hottest topics in the sport, and join the conversation by tweeting us at @golf_com. This week, we discuss Jon Rahm’s future on LIV Golf, the U.S. Amateur at Merion and LeBron James’ move into YouTube golf.

Golf.title: Jack Whaley's U.S. Amateur win, in demanding conditions, was unsurprising
Golf.summary: Englishman Jack Whaley took on an English-style course at the U.S. Amateur, and on Sunday played the final in English-style conditions. The post Jack Whaley’s U.S. Amateur win, in demanding conditions, was unsurprising appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Merion, the club and the course, is about as English as any American thing could be, and Sunday here — for the finale of the 126th U.S. Amateur — was dank and wet and oh-so-English. An Englishman was playing a kid from California. The Englishman won. Not a shocker.

There was something truly great about this Am, the whole seven days of it: six days of hot, dry golf leading to this rainy, cool Sunday; 312 players whittled down to two; and a final featuring two totally dissimilar golfers. Jack Whaley, deeply tanned and powerfully built, grew up in Doncaster, England, plays at Florida State and has a ready-for-the-Tour swing and a grind-it-out demeanor. Jay Leng Jr. grew up in San Diego, plays at Stanford, could not weigh 130 pounds, has a stance wider than Moe Norman’s and a backswing shorter than Jon Rahm’s, and follows no known playbook but his own. It was a delight watching these two go at it in this 36-hole final. Whaley won the match with a birdie on 15, the final nail in his 4-and-3 victory.

Golf.title: McIlroy admits concerns as Scheffler regains winning feeling at St Jude
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy says "he felt lost" as he toils to a 66th-place finish - 25 strokes behind champion Scottie Scheffler - at the St Jude Championship in Memphis.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy says "he felt lost" as he toiled to a 66th-place finish - 25 strokes behind champion Scottie Scheffler - at the St Jude Championship. While world number one Scheffler was a cut above the rest at 17 under overall as he claimed his first victory since January, more concerning for McIlory was that his eight-over total left him ahead of just two players in the first of the three FedEx Cup play-off events.

The Northern Irishman, who won his second Masters title earlier this season had not played competitively since the Open Championship in July. And it told at TPC Southwind, where he failed to record a single round under par across the four days and struggled to find the sort of rhythm that will be needed if he is to claim an unprecedented fourth FedEx Cup later this month.

Golf.body:
It took a little longer than most expected, but Scottie Scheffler has won with TaylorMade’s Qi4D driver. Scheffler ran away from the field Sunday at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, earning his second win of the season and first since the American Express in January.

But for a player who rarely makes equipment changes, the big story is that for the first time in more than three years, Scheffler has won with a driver other than his trusty TaylorMade Qi10 driver. Scheffler surprised many by starting the opening round in Memphis with a new TaylorMade Qi4D driver.

Golf.title: England's Whaley makes history by winning US Amateur
Golf.summary: Jack Whaley becomes only the second Englishman since 1911 to win the US Amateur as he beats American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 at Merion.
Golf.body:
Jack Whaley became only the second Englishman to win the US Amateur Championship since 1911 as he beat American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 in the final at Merion. Victory at the storied course in Pennsylvania gives the 22-year-old from Yorkshire a place in the fields for the Masters, US Open and The Open at St Andrews in 2027.

"I don't think it's sunk in yet," Whaley said when asked about emulating Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, Bryson DeChambeau and Viktor Hovland in winning the prestigious title.

He still can’t break 80, but he’s leaned on his plus-handicap personality to go platinum, his every Bob Does Sports YouTube video commanding seven-figure views, just one arm of an expanding media empire built on good times. Golf.title: LIV Golf player admits breakaway tour might be nearing the end: 'I think time might run out'
Golf.summary: LIV Golf player admits breakaway tour might be nearing the end: 'I think time might run out' Fox News
Golf.body:
Since the Saudi Arabia-backed Public Investment Fund announced they were pulling funding for the LIV Golf Tour at the end of the 2026 season, there's been widespread speculation about the future of the breakaway league.

While LIV initially grabbed big name stars like Bryson DeChambeau, Brooks Koepka, Phil Mickelson and eventually Jon Rahm with big guaranteed contracts and high purses, that momentum seemingly stalled in recent months and years as the league failed to turn a profit. Some younger players, like Michael La Sasso, a recent men's college golf national champion, did forgo the PGA Tour for LIV, but other big names have stayed put.

I started on MySpace doing golf content and modeling content. Golf.title: The problem Rory McIlroy must be wary of with LIV Golf’s future beyond this season in serious doubt
Golf.summary: The problem Rory McIlroy must be wary of with LIV Golf’s future beyond this season in serious doubt hitc.com
Golf.body:
In the months after Rory McIlroy won The Masters in 2025, the Northern Irishman experienced a remarkable slump as he searched for a new golfing purpose. The emotional victory at Augusta National was at least 14 years in the making. Meanwhile, it ended a wait of more than a decade since McIlroy’s fourth major win. It was no surprise, therefore, that the 37-year-old took so long to reassess his goals.

On the course, McIlroy had built his season around the majors and the Ryder Cup for several years. Some PGA Tour and DP World Tour wins obviously meant a lot, but he was clearly aware that they were unlikely to impact his legacy.

Golf.title: His epic streak’s in jeopardy. His valiant charge could keep it alive
Golf.summary: Top PGA Tour pros consider making the Tour Championship a benchmark for a successful season. Sungjae Im has done it every year — until now. The post His epic streak’s in jeopardy. His valiant charge could keep it alive appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There are plenty of ways for professional golfers to define a “successful” season. Is it strokes gained? Top 20s? Wins? Swing feels? Something else? But among top PGA Tour pros, there’s a common refrain: If I’ve made it to East Lake for the Tour Championship, I’ve done something right.

Only 30 pros qualify for the Tour Championship, after all. Those who do are handsomely rewarded with FedEx Cup prize money, a multi-year Tour exemption, a Masters invitation and plenty more. It’s rarefied air, but well earned. Qualifying for East Lake is a testament to season-long excellence.

Golf.title: 'Entire body is shaking': Inside the white-knuckle pressure of U.S. Amateur Saturday
Golf.summary: On U.S. Amateur Saturday at Merion, Jack Whaley and Jay Leng Jr. faced their opponents and a white-knuckle pressure that's unique to the stage. The post ‘Entire body is shaking’: Inside the white-knuckle pressure of U.S. Amateur Saturday appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Jack Whaley crouched down and stared over a putt. It was the type of putt he’d wanted to make his entire life, ever since he started swinging a club at a driving range with his dad in Doncaster, England. The record crowds at Merion murmured as Whaley lined up a four-and-a-half putt for bogey. His lead over Carter Loflin had gone from 3 up to all square in three holes, and he was in danger of letting it all slip away. With the Merion clubhouse behind him, Whaley stared at the biggest putt of his young life — one that would send him to Sunday’s U.S Amateur Championship match and punch his ticket to the 2027 Masters and U.S. Open.

“My entire body is shaking,” Whaley said outside the Merion clubhouse as the sun set on Saturday. “Just got adrenaline pumping through me. That was one of the longest four-foot putts I’ve ever had in my entire life, and there was a lot at stake.”

World number one Scottie Scheffler will take a two-stroke lead into the final round of the St Jude Championship as he chases his first victory since January. Scheffler, 30, carded a two-under 68 on Saturday to sit at 13 under overall, with his American compatriot Sam Burns at 11 under alongside South Korea's Im Sung-jae.

Burns produced a superb bogey-free 62 to move into contention in the FedEx Cup play-off opener at TPC Southwind in Memphis. England's Tommy Fleetwood, who is the defending FedEx Cup champion, is a further three strokes adrift at eight under with Jake Knapp.

Golf.title: The training aid that helped Wyndham Clark win the U.S. Open
Golf.summary: A key training aid helped Wyndham Clark make a vital swing change that was critical in his win at the 2026 U.S. Open. The post The training aid that helped Wyndham Clark win the U.S. Open appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Major championships are won under intense pressure inside the ropes, but their foundation is built on the range. Wyndham Clark’s victory at the 2026 U.S. Open showcased four days of exceptional ball-striking and composure — and was the result of a key swing change that began long before he arrived at Shinnecock Hills.

A key part of that success came from his work with swing coach and GOLF Top 100 Teacher Pat Coyner. Together, they focused on making Clark’s motion more repeatable, starting with his wrist angles, which improved his ability to control the clubface. According to Coyner, one training aid became integral to their work: the ProSENDR.

Golf.title: Merion’s caddies playing essential (and effective) role at this U.S. Amateur
Golf.summary: At the U.S. Amateur at Merion this week, there were 312 players vying for 64 match-play spots. Forty-nine players took Merion caddies. The post Merion’s caddies playing essential (and effective) role at this U.S. Amateur appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — From the first time I set foot at Merion, about 40 years ago, I found myself drawn to the club’s caddies and their stories. My first host at Merion — for lunch in the men’s grill, as it was called then — was a former Merion caddie who became a member, a good local amateur and a prominent lawyer in town. He might have been the first to make the climb from the dank subterranean pen where the caddies used to wait for their loops to the men’s locker room, on the second-floor of the clubhouse, with its shower heads the size of small pizzas. The Merion caddie crew noted this ascension. Later, another Merion caddie, Mike Mayock, the son of a local high school football coach, became a member, an NFL executive and a broadcaster. The Merion caddie crew noted this ascension. The Merion caddie crew is a thing unto itself.

This week, at the U.S. Amateur at Merion, there were 312 players vying for 64 spots in the match-play portion of the event. Forty-nine players took Merion caddies. Said another way, nearly every fulltime summer caddie at Merion, 10 of them college kids, landed a bag in the Am. It’s hard to imagine a more powerful statement about the quality of this eclectic caddie crew.

Golf.title: Ian Poulter admits it may be all over for LIV Golf, ‘I think time might run out’
Golf.summary: Ian Poulter admits it may be all over for LIV Golf, ‘I think time might run out’ Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Ian Poulter joined LIV Golf from the PGA and DP World Tours back in June 2022. Ever since then, Poulter has been one of LIV Golf's most vocal cheerleaders. The 50-year-old Englishman has enjoyed a wonderfully successful career in the game, but he is still waiting for his first victory on LIV.

LIV Golf seems to suit Ian Poulter perfectly at this stage of his career, with fewer events and boisterous crowds in attendance every week. However, the league's future is in doubt right now, despite the recent news that CEO Scott O'Neil has managed to acquire fresh investment ahead of the 2027 season.

Golf.title: LeBron James is joining YouTube Golf. Here's why
Golf.summary: LeBron James is launching a YouTube channel chronicling his newfound golf obsession. Here's why that's a big deal — and a collision of several trends. The post LeBron James is joining YouTube Golf. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Yes, we’re serious. James’ first YouTube video is live as of 10 a.m. ET on Saturday, Aug. 14, kicking off a golf-centric channel chronicling the journey of new obsessive. In some ways, James’ debut video echoes any other buddies’ trip: it’s an epic reunion of old friends in an epic new place, in this case Castle Stuart in Scotland. The difference between his buddies’ trip and yours, though, is that this is a reunion of the 2016 NBA Champion Cleveland Cavaliers. Their collective presence is a reminder of James’ basketball greatness — you’ll recall that 2016 team came back from 3-1 down in the finals to upset the Golden State Warriors — but their chosen reunion activity is a reminder of their shifting priorities: It’s golf season all the time now.

The video, which features James alongside former teammates Kevin Love, J.R. Smith, Richard Jefferson, Tristan Thompson and Channing Frye, was released on James’ inactive-until-now personal YouTube channel, @LeBron. The plan for the channel, per James’ team, is a golf-themed video to be released every month, showcasing James’ journey with the sport, a mix of golf talk, competition, off-course adventure, local culture, food, wine and more.

Golf.title: How to plan an unforgettable Wisconsin golf trip at an affordable price
Golf.summary: I recently went on a golf trip to Wisconsin — and I walked away convinced it's one of the best values in the game. The post How to plan an unforgettable Wisconsin golf trip at an affordable price appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When I moved to Wisconsin eight years ago to work for the Green Bay Packers, I didn’t know much about the Badger state. I’d never seen a snow plow in action and had no clue what a Friday Fish Fry was. I’d never been inside a Festival Foods nor had I tasted a Culver’s ButterBurger. Worst of all, I didn’t realize just how much great golf the state boasted.

Since leaving Wisconsin, I still kick myself for not taking advantage of the abundance of great golf the state has to offer. Luckily, I’ve been able travel back to the midwest in recent years — and I’ve made sure to bring my sticks in an effort to explore all the great golf Wisconsin has to offer.

Golf.title: Inside the Lab: What I learned visiting Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art KOBO facility
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder visited Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art testing facility in Carlsbad to explore a new way of looking at shaft fitting The post Inside the Lab: What I learned visiting Mitsubishi’s state-of-the-art KOBO facility appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Before we got into our testing, we stopped by Mitsubishi’s new KOBO facility in Carlsbad, California. The place is essentially an R&D playground filled with cameras, robots, and custom shaft-testing machines. It gives you a quick look at why what happens in the lab translates directly to finding the center of the face on the golf course.

For decades, the equipment side of the game has leaned on a very tidy, convenient narrative: if you swing fast, you need a heavier, stiffer shaft profile that launches low and kills spin. if you swing slower or struggle to get the ball airborne, you need a lighter, softer shaft that launches high. That makes some sense, but it doesn’t tell the full story.

Golf.title: This 63-year-old went viral at U.S. Amateur. Then went back to work
Golf.summary: Mike McCoy, 63, missed the stroke-play cut at the U.S. Amateur this week but still made a lot of new fans along the way. The post This 63-year-old went viral at U.S. Amateur. Then went back to work appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Sixty-three-old Mike McCoy was never going to win this 126th U.S. Amateur, not when he was giving up 50 yards off the tee to many players in the field, as he did in his two stroke-play rounds alongside 21-year-old U.S. Junior Amateur champion Noah Maclauchlan and 39-year-old U.S. Mid-Amateur champion Brandon Holtz.

The first of those rounds, on Monday, came at Philadelphia Country Club, in Gladwyne, home to a beefy William Flynn design. McCoy made five bogeys and a double and signed for a five-over 75. On Tuesday, he and his partners headed about 6 miles due south for their second round, at storied Merion Golf Club, the star of this week’s show. McCoy had fewer blemishes on his card — three bogeys and a double — en route to a four-over 74. Nine over for 36 holes for the U.S. Senior Amateur champion was a commendable showing but still seven shots more than McCoy needed to join a playoff for a spot in the 64-player match-play field. By Wednesday afternoon, McCoy, who runs an insurance business, was back at his desk in West Des Moines, Iowa.

Golf.title: Do you slice the golf ball? This subtle backswing mistake could be why
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joe Plecker explains the subtle backswing flaw that may be causing you slice — and shows how to fix it. The post Do you slice the golf ball? This subtle backswing mistake could be why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When players come to me fighting a slice, the instinct is almost always to blame the swing. But more often than not, the swing itself is fine — it’s the clubface that’s off. Here’s the pattern I see as a player takes the club back: the face rotates “toe up” relative to their posture. It may look like the club is square (and feels square), but relative to their spine angle at the address, it’s actually open. That small discrepancy is enough to send the ball curving right for a right-handed player.

So, how do we fix this? You can start by trying this simple checkpoint drill. Take an alignment rod and stick it in the ground just behind the ball at address, angled to match your posture. This gives you a visual reference for where the clubface should be pointing as you swing back.

Golf.title: At U.S. Amateur, Merion’s secrets are hiding in a wondrous, windowless room
Golf.summary: Merion’s archives room, in a deep and hidden part of its twist-and-turns clubhouse, is managed by its resident historian, John Capers III. The post At U.S. Amateur, Merion’s secrets are hiding in a wondrous, windowless room appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — If you read Ann Patchett, you will seldom, if ever, encounter the four-letter word that draws you to this website. The author of “Bel Canto” and “Tom Lake” and a current New York Times bestseller, “Whistler,” has plenty of themes in her typing life without ever falling under the spell of ye olde game.

But Patchett’s brother-in-law is a golf pro. And Andy Brennan, the general manager of the bookstore Patchett owns in Nashville, is a golf bum with impeccable credentials. He has actually read John Daly’s “My Life In and Out of the Rough,” just as he has read the Bernard Darwin, Henry Longhurst and Herbert Warren Wind canon. Before he fell into the book business, Brennan was a course superintendent and a course builder. (He once made an ace on one of his own holes.) He has known about a strain of grass called Merion Blue forever, or at least 1971, or circa* 1971. It was in 1971 that Lee Trevino won his U.S. Open at Merion, in a playoff over Jack Nicklaus. Brennan also attended the 1981 U.S. Open at Merion. Classic busman’s holiday**. On Thursday he was back at Merion, for the Am. The U.S. Amateur.

Golf.title: YouTube Golf took over. Tour pros want their piece of the pie, too
Golf.summary: It was only a matter of time before pro golfers joined the YouTube ranks. Here's why they've decided to chase views, too. The post YouTube Golf took over. Tour pros want their piece of the pie, too appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This article first appeared in the July/August issue of GOLF Magazine. In mid-March, the world’s leading golfing content creator — or is it content-creating golfer? — gazed through the windows of the media center at Steyn City, host of that week’s LIV Golf South Africa event in Johannesburg, where a horde of fans were leaning over each other, waiting for his autograph. Bryson DeChambeau had just shot 63, but his eyes said something more. As he waited for his turn at the press conference podium, we chatted for a few minutes — just long enough for him to dream aloud about reuniting professional golf.

The plan he’d devised — constructed, in part, via ChatGPT and Google Gemini — featured tournaments with a field of 104 players: 13 four-man PGA Tour teams competing alongside 13 four-man LIV Golf teams. Half the individual field would be cut after 36 holes — to appease Tiger Woods, DeChambeau said. The new league would be jointly owned by the PGA Tour, LIV and the players. And though it all seems like folly now that LIV may cease to exist in 2027, DeChambeau believed in it so resolutely because of the person he’d convinced of its legitimacy: YouTube CEO Neil Mohan.

Golf.title: This brand has been taking over my closet and they just layered me up
Golf.summary: The new Turtleson collection promises to keep you layered up in style this fall without missing out on the performance you desire. The post This brand has been taking over my closet and they just layered me up appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The fall season is fast approaching, and Turtleson is hoping to keep us all properly layered with new styles to choose from. Turtleson is a large lifestyle clothing brand with a great lineup of golf specific gear, as well as a ton of crossover between the two use cases. My closet has started to get sneaky full with Turtleson gear after I found their gear earlier this season, so let’s take a look at what the new fall collection has to offer.

I have to start off with the new line of 100% Extra Fine Merino Wool items. They sent me a Bex Argyle style hoodie (Yes, hoodie. Yes, it’s awesome) and I really do love it. It’s the kind of layer that makes you feel cozy but not hot. It’s a perfect item for a colder fall morning tee time that leads to a mid-day mild temperature finish without having to feel like you need to take it off and shove it in the bag on the 14th hole. It’s also exceptionally soft and super lightweight.

The rampant uncertainty that has enveloped LIV Golf for months has left many of the league’s biggest names and brightest talents pondering their futures, but some players may be ejected regardless.

With LIV’s team finale in Michigan now cancelled in all but an official statement, the league will convene for the final time in 2026 at the Chatham Hills Club in Indianapolis next week. And lost in the existential talk of LIV’s survival hopes in a post-Saudi era is what, in any typical week, would be a hugely consequential week on the fairways. At the start of the season, LIV increased its relegation positions from six to 11 to prove to the Official World Golf ranking board that the league was not a closed shop.

Golf.body:
Jessica Bang, a promising Australian golfer, has died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage. Bang, who won her first professional event in just her fifth start earlier this year, was preparing for a tournament in Thailand on 1 August when she collapsed.

She was rushed to a hospital in Bangkok and had emergency brain surgery. After being in intensive care for nearly two weeks, she died on Thursday. The WPGA Tour of Australasia said Bang, who turned professional at the end of 2025, was an "outstanding young talent".

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026: ‘I don’t know if she was hurt or it was her strategy’: PV Sindhu after defeat to Wang Zhi Yi
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026: ‘I don’t know if she was hurt or it was her strategy’: PV Sindhu after defeat to Wang Zhi Yi WION
Badminton.body:
PV Sindhu was left to rue a lack of patience in the closing stages after her BWF World Championships campaign ended with a defeat to China's Wang Zhi Yi. Sindhu, who was involved in a closely fought battle, felt the contest was largely under her control but admitted that she could have handled the crucial moments at the end better. “I think in the overall game, especially in the end, I should have been a little more patient,” Sindhu said after the match.

“I can't see any loopholes in between the points. I think in the end especially I should have been a little more patient. That's what I can see from today's game and in the last 3-4 points.” The former world champion was understandably disappointed with the result, particularly after being in contention for much of the match. “Yeah, disappointed of course. Sad about it, I should have converted that. But yeah, I mean that's how it is, that's how sport is,” Sindhu said. “You learn, you lose a lot, you win a lot. I mean when you lose you need to deal with it and bounce back stronger from your mistakes.”

Badminton.title: BWF banks on 15-point games to ease player workload
Badminton.summary: BWF banks on 15-point games to ease player workload Sportstar
Badminton.body:
The Badminton World Federation’s decision to introduce a 15-point scoring system from next season is driven primarily by concerns over player welfare and the increasing physical demands of the sport, Secretary General Thomas Lund said on Thursday. “It’s not a revolution, it’s an evolution of the scoring system,” he said.

Defending the change, he said matches had become longer and tighter as the depth of the sport had increased, meaning even the top players were facing significant physical demands from the opening rounds. “We’re now just tweaking the point system where the load on players will come down, so we actually safeguard the players and their health in a better way.”

One year after he beat Loh Kean Yew at the BWF World Championships 2025, Victor Lai ran into the same opponent – this time in the Round of 16. Remarkably, when he came away after the 22-20 21-18 win, he knew it was the same score by which he had won last time.

Loh had almost run away with the first game with eight straight points, but Lai took it deep and nicked it. In the second he staged a mini-comeback with a display of immaculate control, defence, and opportunistic attack.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Ayush Shetty Exits In Round Of 16, Faces Defeat To Indonesia 2-0
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Ayush Shetty Exits In Round Of 16, Faces Defeat To Indonesia 2-0 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Ayush Shetty exits the men’s singles Round of 16 after losing to Indonesia 2-0 at the BWF World Championships 2026, held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi. The Indian badminton ace, Ayush Shetty, exited the BWF World Championships 2026 in the men’s Round of 16 after losing to the World No.11, Alwi Farhan, in two straight sets. In the latest sports news from Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, Ayush lost to the Indonesian shuttler with 19-21 and 11-21 in 45 minutes. The 21-year-old had a good run at the World Championships as he defeated the World No.1 in men’s singles.

Ayush Shetty came into the court with his two consecutive wins against the World No.1 Shi and Austria’s Filipino. The 21-year-old was cheered on by the crowd at the IG Stadium as he took charge against his opponent with three straight points. In the last meeting between the Indian shuttler and the World No. 11 in 2025, Ayush won 2-1. The game was level till 9-all, with Farhan throwing great smashes at Shetty. The Indonesian shuttler was quick with his strikes, hitting outstanding drop shots. The home player struggled to catch up in the latter half of the set, but he managed to end the set at 19 points. The opening set went to Farhan 21-19 in just 22 minutes.

Badminton.title: Chochuwong Stops Chen Yu Fei
Badminton.summary: Chochuwong Stops Chen Yu Fei BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Pornpawee Chochuwong shook off an unenviable record against Chen Yu Fei to take her place in the quarterfinals of the BWF World Championships 2026. It was a stubborn performance by the Thai, whose only win in 17 matches against the world No.4 had come eight years ago. Today Chochuwong dug in despite fluctuating fortunes in the second game, before staging a comeback from 6-13 in the third to clinch the match 15-21 25-23 21-17 in 84 minutes.

“I’m really happy to beat her because over the last few weeks I was injured at the Japan Open and China Open. I prepared well to play her and it worked,” said Chochuwong. “I just kept running and had to take every single shot she played, so I just had to be patient.

Badminton.title: 'We hope for players' understanding': BWF secy general Lund on India Open
Badminton.summary: 'We hope for players' understanding': BWF secy general Lund on India Open The New Indian Express
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: The India Open tournament has come under scathing criticism because of hazardous pollution in recent years. With player welfare in mind, the Badminton World Federation, while unveiling the 2027-2028 calendar earlier this year, had moved the event by a few weeks to February (2-7). However, that move was just made for the 2027 season and there are still concerns if that shift will bring about any major difference. BWF secretary general Thomas Lund said that they'll be examining all the data in the upcoming months and they are open to exploring all options in the future.

"There's obviously a lot of logistical things when you do these things and we have obviously been in close dialogue around it, the whole calendar and so coming into 2027, it's quite a short space. And for now, it hasn't been possible to totally move out of the first quarter. It is documented that pollution will go down a little bit further into January, February," Lund told reporters on the sidelines of the ongoing BWF World Championships in New Delhi.

Badminton.title: BWF: Synthetic shuttlecocks "inevitable" in badminton, but feathers won't disappear
Badminton.summary: BWF: Synthetic shuttlecocks "inevitable" in badminton, but feathers won't disappear sportstar.thehindu.com
Badminton.body:
The badminton shuttlecock may be on the verge of its biggest change in decades, but the feather is not about to disappear. BWF secretary general Thomas Lund says the federation expects synthetic-feather shuttlecocks to become an increasingly important part of badminton, including at higher levels of competition. But he stressed that the transition will be gradual and dependent on whether manufacturers can produce a shuttle that comes close enough to the performance of the best feather products.

“I think it’s inevitable that we move to a combination between the two,” Lund told Sportstar. “I’m not even sure that we’ll just move to just synthetic feather in years to come.”

Badminton.title: Garret Tan Sparkles on Great Day for Pan Am
Badminton.summary: Garret Tan Sparkles on Great Day for Pan Am BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
The BWF World Championships 2026 continued to throw up big-name casualties, with 14th seed Lakshya Sen falling to world No.92 Garret Tan on a great day for Pan Am. Tan, just 18, ranks No.7 on the World Junior rankings, but made light of the gulf in experience against the home favourite, as he dialled up his attacking game to leave Sen struggling throughout the match. Despite a nasty fall late in the third, Tan kept his composure to deal one of the upsets of the tournament and make his way into the Round of 16.

With compatriots Presley Smith/Jennie Gai and Ishika Jaiswal, and Canada’s Victor Lai and Michelle Li also winning their matches, Pan Am couldn’t have asked for a better day. “I can’t believe I won,” said Tan. “The last couple of tournaments I had the same problem, I was leading and I lost. I didn’t want to think about losing, I just wanted to focus.

Badminton.title: Oldorff beaten in round two to end Finnish run at badminton world championships
Badminton.summary: Oldorff beaten in round two to end Finnish run at badminton world championships Flashscore.com
Badminton.body:
Farhan, a former world youth champion, took victory in straight sets (21–12, 21–9) to progress to the third round - the last 16 stage of the men's singles competition. Having come through a tense three-set match with Vietnam's Le Duc Phat in the first round, a tie with the 11th seed was going to be a tall order for the 23-year-old Finn ranked 48th in the world.

1-1 in the opening set was the last time the two opponents were level, as Farhan gradually built his lead. In the second, Oldorff's hopes were over before they had begun, as he lost the opening 10 points to give himself a mountain to climb, as Farhan cruised to a comfortable victory.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Unnati Hooda Loses To Canada 1-2, Exits Round Of 32
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Unnati Hooda Loses To Canada 1-2, Exits Round Of 32 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Unnati Hooda loses to Canada’s Li in the women’s singles Round of 32 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, ending her run at the BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026. The Indian badminton player, Unnati Hooda, loses to Canada’s Michelle Li in a thrilling battle at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium at the BWF World Championships 2026 in New Delhi. In the latest sports news from Indian badminton, Unnati lost 1-2 in the women’s singles Round of 32 with 21-11, 9-21, and the most intense third set, 21-23, bringing her run at the BWF World Championships 2026 India Open to an end.

Unnati came onto the court with confidence from her previous win against Myanmar, leading with 4 early points. The Canadian shuttler also fought back in the game, matching Hooda at 7-7. However, the 18-year-old charged at Li with 11-8 at half-time. The crowd at the IG Indoor Stadium cheered for Unnati as she took 6 straight points. That was the rather unusual start to Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty's BWF World Championships campaign in New Delhi on Wednesday. Instead, the Scottish pair withdrew before the match. No rallies. No booming Satwik serves. No Chirag interceptions at the net. Just a walkover — and a place in the Round of 16.

Badminton.title: ‘I’ve Got You, Dad!’
Badminton.summary: ‘I’ve Got You, Dad!’ BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
A dream that Malvin Alcala had nurtured for himself over 40 years ago came to fruition when his son Mark Shelley took the court for his debut BWF World Championships. The senior Alcala was a promising player for the Philippines before a back injury in the early 1990s cut short his career and his dream of playing the World Championships and the Olympics. Everything he has done since then – naming his children, for instance, or moving to the USA later – was based around the ambition of seeing them achieve in badminton what he could not.

“This is my dream because it’s my dad’s dream,” said Alcala. “He got injured when he was a player, and he wasn’t able to achieve this dream. So he motivated me. Malvin Alcala was a late entrant to badminton. Raised in a family of modest means (his soldier father had died young), Alcala took up basketball and then stumbled upon badminton when he was 15. Having fallen in love with it and picking up its nuances through observation, he would start winning tournaments a year after he started.

Badminton.title: Turkiye Prevail in Humdinger
Badminton.summary: Turkiye Prevail in Humdinger BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Two mixed doubles pairs who ply their wares on the fringes of the elite circuit produced the most intense match of the day at the BWF World Championships 2026. World No.71 Emre Sonmez/Yasemen Bektas and India’s Ashith Surya/Amrutha Pramuthesh (No.60), were locked in a 71-minute battle that see-sawed all the way before the Turkiye pair became the first from their country to make the second round. The Indians were in the reserves list and promoted to the main draw.

Sonmez and Bektas survived six match points in the second game to take it 30-29, and then saved two more in the third before converting their third opportunity: 16-21 30-29 24-22.

Day Two of Victor Lai’s journey as he preps for the BWF World Championships 2026. After a practice session in the arena, Lai talks about taking note of the conditions, getting a sense of the flight of the shuttle, and the technical adjustments he would have to make.

Today was my second practice in the main hall. Got used to the conditions a bit better today. Very obvious, one side there’s drift: one side is slower and one side’s faster. The side drift’s not crazy strong, but still a little bit… still pretty strong, so a lot of things to be aware of and adapt and a bit of match planning too.
