Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: Kirsty Gilmour's love for badminton knows no bounds. And so does her craze for tattoos. She proudly wears multiple tattoos as they're all close to her heart. The 2019 film version of Little Women, Olympic rings, Mount Fuji, Croissant (to name a few)...each one bears a special meaning — she points at each one with child-like enthusiasm and shares all the relevance behind it.

"This (points at one of her tattoos) is a landscape in Scotland on the northeast coast from Lossiemouth. It's a phone box on the bridge that leads to the beach. Olympic rings for Rio and major medals or titles (...)," she explains, after a practice session ahead of World Championships here.

, badminton's biggest tournament is returning to India with the 2026 edition set to begin at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi. Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: China's best look to maintain rich Worlds history
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: China's best look to maintain rich Worlds history The New Indian Express
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: THE newly-revamped Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium wore a busy look on Saturday as several elite players, including from India and China, hit the courts in the afternoon with a goal to get an edge over their opponents ahead of the BWF World Championships — set to begin on Monday. Even Anders Antonsen, a player who had kept a safe distance from the venue due to pollution over the last three years, was totally immersed in his flicks and returns against Danish counterpart Rasmus Gemke. With coach Irwansyah intently following the proceedings, PV Sindhu also shared the court with Ayush Shetty. Despite the traffic, it was hard to miss players from China.

World No 1 Shi Yu Qi, who is incidentally set to rival Ayush in the opening round, was also involved along with rest of the Chinese stars, as they looked to assess the conditions and make themselves game-ready. And so was Li Shi Feng, China No 2 in men's singles. "I feel like the drift and everything is better than last time. The venue is well-maintained and better than last time," World No 9 Feng said.

Badminton.title: Victor Lai Diary: A Year Ago, Walking on the Clouds
Badminton.summary: Victor Lai Diary: A Year Ago, Walking on the Clouds bwfworldchampionships.bwfbadminton.com
Badminton.body:
There is a trace of wistfulness in Victor Lai’s voice as he recounts his magical week from a year ago at the BWF World Championships 2025. He is of course a far more accomplished player than the version that came to Paris and took down one higher-rated opponent after another, before nearly toppling eventual champion Shi Yu Qi in a sensational semifinal.

So where does the wistfulness come from? “I’d say one thing that might be worse is, last year at the Worlds I had absolutely no pressure, so that feeling of relaxation and that… freedom, I will never feel that freedom again.

Back in 2009, the Worlds were barely a blip on the Indian sporting radar, badminton still a mix of Prakash Padukone-Pullela Gopichand inspired nostalgia and Saina Nehwal induced hope. At the time the bigger talking point wasn't if India would medal or not, it was England pulling out due to a terror threat.

Badminton.title: ‘Good Spirit and Just Hungry for a Medal’
Badminton.summary: ‘Good Spirit and Just Hungry for a Medal’ BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Far from letting his close second round loss at his home BWF World Championships dispirit him, Christo Popov used it as a springboard for a spectacular 12 months. Last year he was close to taking out top seed Shi Yu Qi in the Round of 16 in front of a delirious crowd in Paris; Shi would survive and go on to win the title.

For Popov, there was much to take from that performance. Since then, he has been among the most impressive players on the circuit. He would make history for France in winning the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals; this year would see him win the European Championships, spearhead France into the final of the BWF Thomas Cup, and win his first Super 750 tournament in Japan.

Badminton.title: 2009 to 2026: BWF World Championships return to an India worlds apart
Badminton.summary: 2009 to 2026: BWF World Championships return to an India worlds apart ESPN
Badminton.body:
Starting August 16, 2026, India will play host to the BWF Badminton World Championships for a second time, in circumstances vastly different from the first time the nation hosted it.

Back in 2009, the Worlds were barely a blip on the Indian sporting radar, badminton still a mix of Prakash Padukone-Pullela Gopichand inspired nostalgia and Saina Nehwal induced hope. At the time the bigger talking point wasn't if India would medal or not, it was England pulling out due to a terror threat.

Badminton.title: Men’s Singles: Top Five Players to Watch
Badminton.summary: Men’s Singles: Top Five Players to Watch BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Men’s singles is undergoing a generational shift with a number of young players establishing themselves at the top. While the more experienced ones – such as Chou Tien Chen, Shi Yu Qi and Anders Antonsen, for example – are still top contenders, the number of young stars capable of challenging for the title in 2026 is unprecedented.

This bunch of young stars – names such as Christo Popov, Victor Lai, Alex Lanier, Alwi Farhan and Toma Junior Popov – can be expected to light up the competition. Yet, the older stars have shown that badminton belongs as much to the young and fearless as to the more experienced, craftier type of player.

Badminton.title: Badminton: Delhi battles monkeys and pigeons ahead of BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: Badminton: Delhi battles monkeys and pigeons ahead of BWF World Championships BBC
Badminton.body:
Sports authorities in India are taking extra measures to keep monkeys and pigeons away from a major international badminton tournament in Delhi after wildlife intrusions overshadowed another competition earlier this year.

In January, when India hosted the India Open badminton tournament, organisers had hoped the headlines would be about tense matches, some of the world's best players and the excitement of hosting a major tournament in the capital.
